- **`KhaozEngine.Identity.Oidc` (new, opt-in):** a generic OIDC provider (authorization-code + PKCE via the system browser + a loopback redirect listener) and `OidcTokenValidator` (issuer / audience / lifetime / signature validated against the issuer's discovery doc + JWKS via `Microsoft.IdentityModel`). Works against any compliant issuer (Entra External ID, Google, and the like) by config. `KhaozEngine.Platform` gained a best-effort `Browser.LaunchBrowserAsync`.
- **`KhaozEngine.Identity.Discord` (new, opt-in):** a Discord OAuth2 provider + `DiscordTokenValidator` (userinfo `/users/@me`), for the OAuth2-not-OIDC provider shape. The two backends are opt-in siblings, not bundled in any umbrella; `KhaozEngine.Identity` core is in the Foundation umbrella. Google / Apple / Microsoft presets and OS-keychain token storage are deferred.

## 10.15.0

Game-agnostic objective / goal tracking: a new `KhaozEngine.Objectives` Foundation package so every game hooks one reusable framework for achievements / challenges / quests / dailies instead of building bespoke goal plumbing. Additive (one new package, no removals), so a minor bump; no GPU work. Reference consumer: Nullwake's Challenges system, which pins this to build its point tree on top.

- **`KhaozEngine.Objectives` (new):** the pipeline signals -> counters -> declarative conditions -> completion event. A game `Report(key, amount)`s accumulators and `Observe(key, value)`s peaks for opaque metric-key strings it chose; `ObjectiveTracker` holds a `Persistent` (never resets) and a `Session` counter per key in `MetricScope`, updated together on every report. `ResetScope(MetricScope.Session)` at the game's own run / prestige boundary is the entire "all-time vs single-run" mechanism (the framework never knows what a "run" is). The framework names no domain concept - keys, numeric targets, and scopes only.
- **Declarative objectives:** an `ObjectiveDefinition` is an AND-composition of `ObjectiveCondition`s - `AtLeast(key, target, scope)` (accumulator Sum >=), `Reached(key, target, scope)` (peak Max >=, for "reach depth N"), `AtMost(key, target, scope)` (constraint / negative goal). Each key holds both a Sum (fed by Report) and a Max (fed by Observe), so one key backs both an accumulator and a peak goal unambiguously. Objectives are indexed by the keys their conditions watch, so a report re-evaluates only the objectives touching the changed key, never the full set (the perf contract for thousands of reports/sec against hundreds of objectives).
- **Completion:** `ObjectiveTracker.ObjectiveCompleted` fires once when all of an objective's conditions hold; idempotent (completes once, stays completed, never re-fires) and survives Capture/Restore. Rewards / points / trees stay entirely game-side via an opaque `Metadata` payload echoed back on `ObjectiveCompletion.Metadata` (e.g. a `tier:hard` tag), which the framework never inspects.
- **Deterministic + presentation-free + persistence-agnostic:** pure counters + predicates, no RNG / wall-clock (matters for a balance sim); single-threaded sim assumption documented. Display text is a `StringId` (optional localized `Name` / `Description`), never a raw literal - the only dependency is `KhaozEngine.App`. `Capture()` returns a plain `ObjectivesSnapshot` (deterministic order) the game serializes into its own save; `Restore()` reloads it and surfaces any objective a patched-in challenge already satisfies. `GetProgress` / `GetAllProgress` expose per-objective completion + per-condition (current, target) for a progress log without game-side bookkeeping. No JSON in core. In the `Foundation` umbrella (so also reachable from `Game2D` / `Game3D` / `Server`).

## 10.14.0

Server-authoritative currency wallet: a new `KhaozEngine.Commerce` package family for money-safe, idempotent currency balances keyed by a verified account identity the consumer supplies. Additive (three new packages, no removals), so a minor bump; no GPU work.

- **`KhaozEngine.Commerce` (new):** the identity-agnostic wallet core. `IWalletStore` is a transactional seam over an append-only ledger plus a materialized balance, with atomic `CreditAsync` / `DebitAsync` that are idempotent per `(account, currency, idempotencyKey)` (a replayed key credits once and returns the balance as of the original operation) and reject overspend as a result flag, never a throw. Ships `InMemoryWalletStore` (dependency-free reference and test backend). `Wallet` maps a product catalog (`IProductCatalog` / `ProductDefinition`) to credits and redeems a `VerifiedEntitlement` idempotently by source transaction id; `IEntitlementValidator` is the money-in seam (concrete store/processor validators are deferred). `AccountId` / `CurrencyId` are opaque validated value types, and auth is the consumer's seam (no `Netcode` dependency). Depends only on `KhaozEngine.Progression`.
- **`PeriodicGrant` (in `KhaozEngine.Commerce`):** a server-clock daily/periodic reward built on `WallClockRewardSchedule` and an `IGrantScheduleStore`, routed through the wallet so it is non-stacking and credited exactly once. The server instant is the only clock, so it is immune to client clock tampering.
- **`KhaozEngine.Commerce.Sqlite` / `KhaozEngine.Commerce.SqlServer` (new, opt-in):** SQL backends for `IWalletStore` + `IGrantScheduleStore`, raw parameterized ADO.NET mirroring the `WorldStore` backend split (schema created on construction, idempotency via a composite unique index on `(account_id, currency_id, idempotency_key)`, atomic balance updates in a serializable transaction). Not bundled in the `Server` umbrella. The SQL Server backend's tests are gated on `KE_COMMERCE_SQLSERVER`; run them against a live server before first real-money use.

## 10.13.0

Gui widget parity for retained settings/dialog UI: the retained `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextInput`, and `PopupPanel` gain the fade, programmatic, and scrolling affordances a consumer previously had to reimplement locally, all additive and default-off/no-op so every existing consumer renders byte-identically. Minor bump (no removals); no GPU golden rebake (the new paths only bite when their opt-in knobs are set, verified by the headless widget tests + full suite on Metal).

- **Uniform `Opacity` fade (`KhaozEngine.Gui`):** `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextInput`, and `PopupPanel` each expose a `float Opacity = 1f` that scales every drawn colour's alpha at draw time (via the existing `GuiDraw.WithOpacity`), so a host transition can fade the whole widget in/out. Mirrors the existing `Dropdown.Opacity`; default 1 is a no-op.
- **`PopupPanel` scrolling + layout (`KhaozEngine.Gui`):** a new `Update(Pointer, float wheelDelta)` overload adds wheel + drag-to-scroll over content that overflows the (auto-sized, max-height-clamped) panel, scissor-clipped, with a read-only `ScrollOffset` and a tunable `ScrollWheelSpeed`. The two footer buttons now shrink to share the row on a narrow panel (wide panels keep the fixed 130-unit width, so their geometry is unchanged). `SetRows` is now a no-op when the rows are value-equal, so calling it every frame no longer resets an in-progress scroll.
- **`PopupPanel` opt-in content extras (`KhaozEngine.Gui`):** `WrapLongLabels` (default false) word-wraps a stat row whose value is empty across the content width (the row grows to fit, via `TextLayout.Wrap`); `PopupRow.Stat(label, value, valueColor, iconColor)` takes an optional colour swatch drawn before the label (`IconSize` sizes it). Both are additive; a row without them draws exactly as before.
- **`TextInput` programmatic + localized API (`KhaozEngine.Gui`):** `SetText(value)` replaces the buffer (clamped to `MaxLength`, surfaced as a `TextChanged` on the next `Update`); `Focus()` / `Unfocus()` are now public. The placeholder is `LocalizedText` via a new `PlaceholderContent` (the `Placeholder` string is now an `[Obsolete]` shim, matching `PopupPanel.Title`).
- **`Toggle.WasToggled` / `Slider.WasChanged` (`KhaozEngine.Gui`):** frame-flag mirrors of the respective `Update` return value, for callers that drive the widget and inspect the result later in the frame rather than at the call site.
- **Showcase** migrates its `TextInput` placeholder to a localized `Widgets.NamePlaceholder` catalog string (the old raw literal moved off the now-obsolete `Placeholder` setter).

## 10.12.0

DPI-aware, native-resolution UI rendering: a point-space UI layer that stays crisp on HiDPI / non-integer window scales, so text and vector chrome rasterize at device-pixel density instead of being fractionally magnified. The design canvas still letterboxes the game field; the UI is now decoupled to render in logical points (1 point = the DPI scale in device pixels) and reflows to the window rather than scaling. Additive API (no removals), so a minor bump; existing design-space rendering is byte-identical (device-pixel snapping is opt-in via the point-space viewport), so no GPU golden rebake was needed (verified on Metal).

- **`DpiFont` (new, `KhaozEngine.Render2D`):** a logical-size font that bakes its atlas at the live DPI scale and re-bakes only when that scale changes (stable per display, so not per window resize). Call `font.For(frame.DpiScale)` each frame and draw the returned `SpriteFont` 1:1 in a point-space pass. Create via `Render2DSurface.LoadDpiFont(...)` / `LoadDefaultDpiFont(...)` (and the snapshot context). Backed by `SpriteFont`'s new fractional bake **density** (atlas at `pixelHeight*density`, `RenderScale = 1/density`, layout metrics unchanged; the integer `oversample` form delegates and is byte-identical at density 1).
- **`UiViewport` (new, `KhaozEngine.Windowing`):** a point-space `IDesignViewport` where authoring units are logical points and the scale is the DPI factor (no letterbox); Width/Height track the logical window, so it reflows on resize. Drops into `SpriteBatch.Begin`, `Pointer.Update`, `ComputeScissor`, and the Gui screens/layout unchanged. Drive it with `UiViewport.Update(Frame)`.
- **`Frame.DpiScale` + `Frame.LogicalWidth`/`LogicalHeight` (new):** the logical window size (points) and device-pixels-per-point (`Width/LogicalWidth`), exposed so a game can bake/snap the UI to the live DPI.
- **Device-pixel snapping (`KhaozEngine.Render2D` / `KhaozEngine.Primitives`):** `ViewportMath.SnapToDevicePixel`/`SnapRectToDevice`/`SnapLengthToDevice` (pure), and `SpriteBatch.DeviceScale`/`DeviceOffset`/`SnapRect`/`SnapLength`. `SpriteBatch` snaps glyph origins and `GuiDraw` snaps widget rects + border thickness, but **only inside a point-space pass** - gated by a new `IDesignViewport.SnapsToDevicePixels` (default false; `UiViewport` true), so design-space / world / screen rendering is byte-identical (a borderless style stays borderless).
- **`GameApp` point-space UI pass (`KhaozEngine.Game`):** a per-frame `UiViewport Ui` + `Pointer UiPointer`, plus a new `OnDrawUi(SpriteBatch)` pass (a second `Begin(Ui)/End` after `OnDraw2D`) routed through `SceneManager.DrawUi` / `GameScene.OnDrawUi`. Empty by default, so games that only use `OnDraw2D` are unaffected; author DPI-aware, reflowing UI here and hit-test with `UiPointer`.
- **Showcase** adopts it: the landing menu (title, row buttons, hint) and the display-settings readout now draw through the point-space pass with `DpiFont`s, so their text is crisp on HiDPI and the row buttons wear uniform device-pixel-snapped borders.

## 10.11.0

New crisp default GUI look and a central `GuiTheme`, plus semantic button presets. **The out-of-box widget appearance changed**: the flat blue-grey default is replaced by a modern neutral-dark palette with a blue accent, subtle 3px corners, and 1px hairline borders (no shadow/gradient/glow). To keep the old look, set `GuiTheme.Default = GuiTheme.Legacy;` at startup (before building widgets), or set `button.Style = GuiStyle.Legacy` per button. Additive API (no removals), so a minor bump, but re-pinning shifts the look of any game that uses the engine widget defaults.

- **`GuiTheme` (new struct):** the single semantic palette every retained widget reads (`Background`, `Surface`/`SurfaceHover`/`SurfacePress`/`SurfaceDisabled`, `Border`/`BorderHover`/`BorderDisabled`, `Accent`/`AccentBright`, `Text`/`TextMuted`/`TextDisabled`, `Danger`/`DangerBright`, `CornerRadius`, `BorderThickness`). Ambient `GuiTheme.Default` (the crisp `GuiTheme.Crisp`) is settable once at startup to rebrand the whole UI; widgets capture it at construction. `GuiTheme.Legacy` reproduces the old aesthetic.
- **`GuiStyle.Default` is now crisp** (subtle 3px radius, hairline border, accent-tinted, no bloom) and equals the new `GuiStyle.Primary`. `GuiStyle.Modern` (rounded + glow + shadow) is unchanged and now builds from `GuiStyle.Legacy`, so its GPU goldens (`scene2d_modern`, `gui_button_glow`) are byte-frozen.
- **Semantic presets (new `GuiStyle` statics):** `Primary` (accent, == Default), `Secondary` (muted surface), `Danger` (red), `Active` (bright-accent selected). Pass to `Button`/`GuiSurface.Button` etc.
- **`GuiStyle.Legacy` (new):** the exact pre-10.11.0 flat blue-grey button style, for a byte-exact old Button.
- **Retained widgets restyled:** `Button`/`Toggle`/`Slider`/`Dropdown`/`Panel` (and `TextInput`/`PopupPanel`/`ScrollablePanel` via `Style`) default their colours from `GuiTheme.Default` and pick up the 3px/hairline treatment, so the whole set is crisp with no per-widget config.
- **Showcase** restyled to the new look and demos the four semantic button variants (the "Gui" room, immediate-mode screen).
- No GPU golden rebake was needed (goldens render `Modern` + raw primitives, never a default-styled widget; verified on Metal). Consumers re-pin to adopt; use `GuiTheme.Legacy` to keep the old look.

## 10.10.0

`ScreenStack` now owns and exposes a shared `InputManager`, so the retained UI path can actually drive `FocusNavigator` and the 10.9.0 keyboard/gamepad widget overloads. Until now the retained path (`ScreenStack`/`Screen`) only carried an `InputState` + `Pointer` and never an `InputManager`, so `FocusNavigator.Update(InputManager)` and `Toggle`/`Slider`/`Dropdown` `Update(InputManager, focused)` had no manager to feed from inside a `Screen` (an `InputManager` was constructed only in tests). Additive API, so a minor bump.

- **`ScreenStack.InputManager`** (new): the shared high-level input manager driving the stack (menu nav + action mapping + the composed pointer), updated every frame from the routed `InputState` (and viewport). Screens read it as `Manager.InputManager` to drive a `FocusNavigator` and the keyboard/gamepad widget overloads.
- **`ScreenStack.Pointer` is now the manager's pointer.** `Pointer` changed from a standalone instance to `=> InputManager.Pointer` (same lifetime, same per-frame `Update(input, viewport)`), so a screen can freely mix pointer-only widget updates (`Update(Manager.Pointer)`) and manager-driven ones (`Update(Manager.InputManager, focused)`) and the click-through `BlockRegion` gate still composes across all of them (one pointer, not two). Behaviour of the pointer itself is unchanged; `ScreenStack.Input` (the raw `InputState`) is unchanged and also reachable as `InputManager.State`.
- **Showcase settings screen wired as the reference.** `KhaozEngine.Showcase`'s `SettingsScreen` now drives its volume `Slider` + fullscreen `Toggle` with a `FocusNavigator` over `Manager.InputManager` (Up/Down moves the focused row, Left/Right adjusts, Enter flips, Esc backs out), with a focus ring on the active row. Pointer still works on every row. This is the pattern a game uses instead of wrapping each control in a `MenuEntry` shell.
- No breaking changes. Consumers re-pin to adopt; existing screens that only use `Manager.Pointer` are unaffected.

## 10.9.0

Keyboard/gamepad navigation for the retained `Toggle`, `Slider`, and `Dropdown` widgets, so a settings row can be driven without a pointer and no longer needs the `MenuEntry` shell to be focusable. Additive and opt-in: every existing `Update(Pointer)` overload is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the new input reads only through `InputManager` menu actions (no raw window input, headless-testable). Additive API, so a minor bump.

- **Wired convenience overload on each widget:** `Update(InputManager input, bool focused, PlayerIndex? player = null)` layers keyboard/gamepad on top of the pointer path, mirroring `FocusNavigator.Update(InputManager)`. Only when `focused` does it read menu actions; `player` scopes gamepad input (null = any). Returns true if the widget changed this frame by either path.
  - `Toggle`: menu-select (Enter/Space/A/Start) flips; "select next" (Right/D-pad right) forces on; "select previous" (Left/D-pad left) forces off.
  - `Slider`: "select next/previous" nudges `Value` by the new `NudgeStep` field (default 0.1); the pointer drag is unchanged.
  - `Dropdown`: closed, menu-select opens and "select next/previous" cycles the selection in place; open, menu-up/down move the highlight, menu-select commits it, menu-cancel (Escape/B/Back) closes without changing.
- **Pure primitives (headless, pointer-independent), matching `Slider.Nudge`:** `Toggle.Flip()` / `Toggle.Set(bool)`; `Dropdown.Open()` / `Close()` / `HighlightNext()` / `HighlightPrevious()` / `CommitHighlight()` / `StepSelection(int)`. Each fires the existing change callback / sets `WasChanged` and returns whether it changed. Consumers wanting custom key bindings can drive these directly.
- **New `Dropdown` state for keyboard use:** `HighlightedIndex` (the open-list cursor; -1 when no keyboard highlight is active), a `Wrap` flag (default true - movement wraps at the ends, matching `FocusNavigator`), and a `FocusColor` for the highlighted row. `DrawOverlay` fills the highlighted row with `FocusColor`. The pointer-only path never activates the highlight (`HighlightedIndex` stays -1), so its overlay draw stays byte-identical to pre-10.9.0.
- **`Slider` gains `NudgeStep`** (default 0.1) as the per-step delta for the wired overload; the existing `Nudge(float)` primitive is unchanged.
- Consumers re-pin to adopt. A settings screen can now feed each row's widget the frame's `InputManager` with a `focused` flag from a `FocusNavigator` instead of routing through `MenuEntry`. No breaking changes.

## 10.8.0

Fixes macOS in-place self-update, which could never complete: the applier now re-seals the `.app` bundle after the file swap and before the code-signature verify. On macOS the game ships as a signed `.app` whose `_CodeSignature/CodeResources` seal covers every file, so the in-place swap of the staged payload inside `Contents/MacOS/` invalidated the seal and the fail-closed `codesign --verify --deep --strict` the applier runs afterward ALWAYS failed, rolling every macOS update back (only `win-x64`/`linux-x64` self-updated). Additive API, so a minor bump.

- **New seam member.** `IUpdaterEnvironment` gains `bool ResealCodeSignature(string executablePath)`, a default interface member returning `true` (a no-op success for platforms without bundle sealing and for external implementers predating it, same source-compatible style as the 10.6.0 `ReplaceFile`/`TryRelaunch` additions). `UpdateApplier.Apply` calls it after the swap and after the quarantine clear, immediately before `VerifyCodeSignature`; a `false` result rolls the update back and relaunches the old version exactly like a verify failure (fail-closed), before the manifest is committed, so the old binaries + old manifest stay consistent.
- **Real re-seal is ad-hoc, inner-to-outer.** `SystemUpdaterEnvironment.ResealCodeSignature` re-signs the enclosing `.app` with `codesign --force --sign -` (ad-hoc, the only key an end-user Mac has - only CI holds the Developer ID private key), signing nested Mach-O libraries (`*.dylib`/`*.so`) and framework/helper bundles deepest-first, then the top bundle with `--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags`. It does NOT use `codesign --deep` (Apple deprecates it for signing). This rebuilds `CodeResources` so the verify passes; the ad-hoc seal drops Developer ID / notarization, which is acceptable because the updater has already cleared quarantine and the app has already launched, so Gatekeeper's quarantined-first-launch gate is past. Off macOS it is a no-op returning `true`. Any `codesign` failure returns `false` (fail-closed).
- **Companion consumer work (NOT in this release).** For a game's macOS head to self-update, its publish CI must Developer ID sign + notarize the ORIGINAL bundle so the very first launch passes Gatekeeper (a freshly downloaded unsigned bundle is quarantined-blocked before the updater ever runs). The engine re-seal closes the engine half; the signing/notarization is per-game CI work. See `docs/UPDATER.md`.
- Orthogonal to the 10.6.0 atomic-swap + relaunch-retry work (torn images + the Windows relaunch race); this is only the macOS bundle seal. Consumers re-pin to adopt.

## 10.7.1

Fixes the decel-to-stop FACING glitch that the 10.7.0 position fix left behind: the local avatar's model briefly spun to face backward/sideways for a few frames before correcting when it came to a stop. `ReplicatedCharacterAnimators` derives facing from the render-position delta, and after a stop the rendered position still settles with a tiny residual sag (backward for a few frames, then forward); that delta reads as motion reversing direction, so the facing chased it. Facing now gates on the exact planar speed too (`CharacterSample.PlanarSpeed`, when supplied) as well as the derived heading magnitude, so at a real stop (exact speed 0) the yaw holds through the settle instead of spinning. The heading DIRECTION is still taken from the derived velocity (exact speed is magnitude-only); remotes (no exact speed) are unchanged - they gate on the derived speed alone and do not have the local avatar's client-ahead settle. Behaviour-only, no API change. Consumers that already pass the 10.7.0 exact-speed `CharacterSample` get the facing fix for free; re-pin to adopt.

## 10.7.0

Fixes the decel-to-stop reconcile shake: when the local player stopped (walk or sprint) the avatar and follow camera visibly jittered back-and-forth for a moment as the position settled, and the locomotion animation flickered walk<->idle. Reproducible on loopback, so it was local-prediction render-continuity on the stop transition, not latency. `KhaozEngine.Netcode`'s render smoothing is the source fix (behaviour-only, no API change); `KhaozEngine.Game.Render3D` adds an optional exact-speed input so the animation state can be driven off the clean commanded speed (additive API, so a minor bump; consumers re-pin to adopt - Ruinborne bundles it into its held player update).

- **Root cause.** A client running ahead of the server crosses a genuine authority dip at a velocity transition: it stops instantly in its own prediction, but the authority is an input-RTT (~1-2 ticks, even on loopback) behind and is still applying the pre-stop moves, so the basis the client reconciles against dips BACKWARD for a tick or two and then catches up (a real per-tick correction, not jitter). The `9.23.0` C1 reconcile kept `previousPredictedPosition` pinned while only the target rebased, which was correct for a STEADY (matching) rebase but, on a backward rebase, left the inter-tick lerp interpolating toward the dipped-back target - dragging the rendered position backward within half a tick. The decaying render offset added a second, overshooting reversal on the recovery.
- **`ClientPrediction` render smoothing (behaviour change, no public API change).** The C1 reconcile now TRANSLATES the whole inter-tick segment (`previousPredictedPosition -> predictedState`) by the rebase delta, so the segment's VELOCITY is preserved (zero for a stopped player) and the entire target jump is absorbed into the render offset instead of being chased by the interpolation. A matching rebase has a zero delta, so the `9.23.0` steady-run behaviour (the fixed 30 Hz camera sawtooth) is unchanged. The planar render offset now decays with a critically-damped (velocity-carrying) filter instead of a first-order exponential, with its velocity reset on each re-anchor: the inertia holds the render steady through the transient authority dip, and the reset kills a secondary overshoot when the target recovers and the offset flips sign. The vertical axis (jump/fall) keeps its first-order decay (no comparable transient-dip failure mode). Net: the reversal (~55% of a tick, a sharp two-frame back-and-forth) becomes a smooth sag under ~13% of a tick, within the existing 0.03 m correction dead-zone, at every render:tick ratio. `LocalHorizontalSpeed` / `PredictedHorizontalSpeed` were already clean (commanded-path only) and are unaffected.
- **`ReplicatedCharacterAnimators` exact planar-speed input (additive).** New `CharacterSample` constructor `(id, position, isLocal, grounded, verticalVelocity, planarSpeed)` and `HasPlanarSpeed` / `PlanarSpeed` members. When supplied, the planar speed drives the idle/walk/run locomotion state and the clip-speed sync DIRECTLY instead of being finite-differenced from the rendered position, so the local avatar's animation no longer strobes walk<->idle on the stop transition. Pass `WorldClient.LocalHorizontalSpeed`. Facing still follows the derived heading (the exact speed is magnitude-only). The position-only and exact-grounded/vertical constructors are unchanged; remotes (position only) keep the windowed position-derived speed. The `RoomNet` showcase adopts it for its local player.

## 10.6.0

`KhaozEngine.Updates` hardens the Windows post-apply relaunch against the antivirus / file-lock race that could crash the auto-relaunched game with "unable to start correctly (0xc0000142)" right after an update, then recover only on the next launch. The copy path was already resilient (40-retry lock wait); this makes the relaunch path resilient too. Additive public API (new `RelaunchStartupOutcome` enum, two default interface members, new `UpdateApplier` constants), so a minor bump; consumers re-pin to adopt.

- **Relaunch retry (the definitive load-ready gate).** New `IUpdaterEnvironment.TryRelaunch(exe, dir, watchMs)` returning `RelaunchStartupOutcome` (`Running` / `StartupFailed` / `ExitedEarly` / `LaunchError`): the real environment starts the game, watches it briefly, and reports whether it survived. `UpdateApplier` runs a watch-and-retry loop (`RelaunchMaxAttempts = 8`, `RelaunchWatchMilliseconds = 2500`, capped growing back-off) that retries only a fast startup-failure NTSTATUS or a launch error, so an antivirus minifilter still blocking *execution* of the freshly-written image (openable-for-a-handle is necessary but insufficient) is waited out instead of surfacing as a crash dialog. A process that survives the watch, or ran and exited on its own, is done; a genuine managed crash is not retried. If every attempt fails the update still stands - only the auto-relaunch is abandoned (logged), so the next start picks up the new version.
- **Atomic swap.** New `IUpdaterEnvironment.ReplaceFile(source, destination)`: the real environment copies to a temp file in the destination's directory then renames it into place (a same-volume rename is atomic), so the on-disk file - the game exe included - is only ever the complete old or complete new image, never a half-written one the relaunch could load. This closes the "WER reports the *old* version" torn-image tell. The install-file copy loop now routes through it (retried on a sharing violation like the old in-place copy).
- **Strengthened pre-relaunch gate.** Delivered by the combination: the atomic swap guarantees the image is never half-written, the existing settle poll (`CanOpenExclusively`) proves it is no longer locked, and the new launch-verify-and-retry proves it is actually executable. The settle poll is documented as a necessary-but-insufficient first-line pre-filter; the relaunch retry is the real gate.
- **Relaunch is logged.** Every attempt (`Relaunch attempt n/8: <exe>`), its outcome, each back-off wait, and the final give-up now go to `updater.log`. The relaunch was previously an unlogged blind spot, making the whole failure invisible in logs.
- **The "Finishing" progress window stays visible across the relaunch-retry wait** (Windows), so the user sees the marquee instead of a bare OS error dialog; it closes once the game is launched or the retry budget is spent. New default interface members (`ReplaceFile`, `TryRelaunch`) keep external `IUpdaterEnvironment` implementers source-compatible.
- Ships in Hardpoint, SpaceGame, Ruinborne, Nullwake (all pin their own version and re-pin to adopt).

## 10.5.0

New package `KhaozEngine.Progression` (in the `Foundation` umbrella): `WallClockRewardSchedule`, a pure primitive for "every N of real-world time a reward becomes available and stays available until claimed", immune to game `TimeScale` and to offline catch-up caps. Additive (a brand-new zero-dependency package), so a minor bump.

- **New package `KhaozEngine.Progression`** - GPU-free, zero third-party dependencies, added to the `KhaozEngine.Foundation` umbrella. A home for wall-clock progression primitives.
- **`WallClockRewardSchedule` (readonly struct).** Two serializable values - `Interval` (`TimeSpan`) and `NextAvailableUtc` (`DateTimeOffset`) - and pure time math over an explicitly-passed `nowUtc`, so availability is measured against real wall-clock time and is completely immune to game `TimeScale` and to offline / time-skip catch-up caps. No ambient clock: the caller passes `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` in production and a fixed instant in tests.
  - `IsAvailable(nowUtc)` - `nowUtc >= NextAvailableUtc`.
  - `TimeUntilAvailable(nowUtc)` - remaining wall-clock time, clamped to `TimeSpan.Zero` once available (never negative), for a HUD countdown.
  - `Claim(nowUtc)` - **non-stacking**: consumes the single available reward and schedules the next one exactly one `Interval` after the claim instant, so being away for many intervals still yields one reward, not a stacked backlog.
  - `Start(interval, nowUtc, TimeSpan initialDelay)` + a `Start(interval, nowUtc, bool availableImmediately = false)` convenience overload. The `initialDelay` overload is the **first-run knob** (called out rather than hard-coded): `TimeSpan.Zero` for an immediate welcome reward, `interval` for a full period, or a random `0..interval` offset so the first reward does not always land on the full-interval boundary (RNG stays in the caller).
- **Persistence-agnostic.** The consumer stores the plain `NextAvailableUtc` timestamp (interval usually from config) in its own save and reconstructs the struct on load. All timestamps are normalised to UTC - a local-offset instant is *converted* via `ToUniversalTime()`, never relabelled - so a schedule round-trips through serialization without drifting.
- **Clock-step safe.** A backward wall-clock step or an implausibly far-future timestamp can neither brick the schedule (arithmetic saturates at `DateTimeOffset.MinValue`/`MaxValue` instead of overflowing) nor spam rewards (it's a persistent boolean threshold, not an event). `Start` rejects a non-positive interval or a negative initial delay.
- **Tests.** New headless `WallClockRewardScheduleTests` (13 cases): available at/after the interval and not before, immediate-mode and initial-delay-offset seeding, first-run full-interval seeding, claim advances by exactly one interval, non-stacking after a long absence, backward-clock no-op, overflow clamp near `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue`, local-offset-to-UTC conversion (never relabelled), the zero-when-available countdown, and the `Start` argument validation.
- Docs: new `KhaozEngine.Progression/README.md`; `README.md` gains the package-table row and lists Progression in the `Foundation` umbrella row + repo layout; `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` gains a "Wall-clock periodic rewards" section; the `CLAUDE.md` layering note lists the new leaf.

## 10.4.1

Ports the 9.32.1 pending-task hygiene fix from `WorldPersistence` to its sibling `CellPersistence` (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`): a faulted or canceled background store task no longer accumulates unpruned, so a store outage can't grow the pending list unbounded or make the documented boot sequence (`LoadMeta -> Preload -> Flush`) / the shutdown flush throw. Bug-fix + behaviour hardening; no API change beyond the additive `OnStoreError` event.

- **`CellPersistence.Update` now prunes every finished task, not just `RanToCompletion`.** A new `PrunePending` (mirroring `WorldPersistence.PrunePending`) removes completed tasks, observes each faulted/canceled one (`Task.Exception.GetBaseException()`), and surfaces it through the new **`public event Action<Exception>? OnStoreError`** raised OUTSIDE `pendingLock`. Previously a faulted cell save, meta write, or 9.33.0 quarantine write stayed in `pending` forever and `FlushAsync`'s `Task.WhenAll` rethrew it.
- **`FlushAsync` (via `AwaitPendingAsync`) no longer throws on a store fault.** It awaits every tracked task to completion, then surfaces each faulted/canceled task through `OnStoreError` instead of rethrowing the first via `Task.WhenAll`, so the boot sequence and the shutdown flush complete cleanly through a store outage.
- **A faulted cell save now stays dirty and retries.** `SaveDirtyPass` advances the per-cell `lastSaved` baseline only AFTER the write lands (moved into a new `SaveCellAsync`); the old code set it before the save, so a faulted save was silently treated as persisted and never retried. The meta write got the same treatment (`SaveMetaAsync`, interlocked because the continuation runs off the server thread), so a faulted meta write is also retried on a later pass.
- **A faulted quarantine write is surfaced and dropped, not retried.** The one-shot forensic copy is fire-and-forget (tracked only so a flush can observe it); the cell has already started fresh, so a fault leaves the load path unaffected and there is nothing worth the retry bookkeeping.

## 10.4.0

The Gui text sinks take an optional `scale`, so a game that draws one shared font at many sizes (SpaceGame does this for pixel-parity) can render scaled Gui text without a per-size font. Additive with every parameter defaulting to `1f`, so a minor bump and every existing caller stays byte-identical.

- **`GuiSurface` text sinks gain a trailing `float scale = 1f`.** `Label(SpriteFont, LocalizedText, Vector2, Vector4, float scale = 1f)` forwards straight to the scale-capable `SpriteBatch.DrawString`. `Label(SpriteFont, Rect, LocalizedText, Vector4, GuiAlign = Center, float scale = 1f)` scales the measured text so the horizontal alignment and vertical centring stay correct. `Button(SpriteFont, Rect, LocalizedText, GuiStyle, bool enabled = true, bool selected = false, float scale = 1f)` scales the label only - the rect and the press-origin hit-test are unchanged. `StatChip(..., float scale = 1f)` scales its label/value line. The obsolete raw-`string` and `[LocalizationStringSink]` overloads are untouched (they forward at the default scale), and the KELOC analyzer is unchanged.
- **Retained `Label` gains a `public float Scale = 1f;`** applied in `Draw` for both the single-line and the word-wrapped paths (glyphs, advances, line height, and the wrap width all scale together).
- **`Render2D.TextLayout` grows an optional `scale`** on `AlignedX`, `DrawAligned`, and `DrawWrapped` (the retained-label draw path). The measured width, wrap width, and line advance all multiply by the scale; `scale = 1` reproduces the previous layout exactly.
- **New shared helper `GuiDraw.AlignedTextPos(Rect, Vector2 measured, float lineHeight, GuiAlign, float scale = 1f, float pad = 0f)`** - the single source of truth for placing a scaled, aligned, vertically-centred line inside a rect, used by both `GuiSurface.Label(Rect, ...)` and `GuiDraw.DrawButton` (which itself takes the new trailing `scale`).
- **Tests.** New headless `GuiTextScaleTests` cover the pure positioning math: `AlignedTextPos` reproduces the old centred layout exactly at `scale = 1`, scales the measured width and line height at `scale = 2`, and honours pad on left/right; `TextLayout.AlignedX` matches between the defaulted and explicit `scale = 1` and scales the width at `scale = 2`. The scaled draw itself is already covered on-device by `DrawStringScaleGpuTests`.
- Docs: `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` gains a "scaling Gui text" note; the `KhaozEngine.Gui` and `KhaozEngine.Render2D` package READMEs mention the new `scale` parameters.

## 10.3.0

KELOC now guards the low-level `SpriteBatch.DrawString` text sink, not just the Gui widgets, so games that render their UI straight through the 2D primitive (SpaceGame does this for its whole UI) are no longer invisible to localization enforcement. Additive (a new opt-in analyzer diagnostic, no API change), so a minor bump.

- **New diagnostic `KELOC003` (Warning): a bare string literal drawn straight to `Render2D.SpriteBatch.DrawString`.** It fires on a call to the engine primitive `KhaozEngine.Render2D.SpriteBatch.DrawString(font, "text", ...)` whose text argument is a non-interpolated, non-verbatim string literal of length > 1 that contains a letter. Interpolated text (`$"Score {n}"`), variables, numbers, format tokens (`"{0}"`), and single-character glyphs are deliberately left alone, so `DrawString`'s constant use for numbers, names, and debug output does not become a false positive. `DrawString` keeps its `string` parameter (retyping such a hot primitive to `LocalizedText`, and resolving a catalog at draw time, is not its job), so this is a Roslyn diagnostic rather than a compile error, mirroring how `KELOC002` already keys off `LocalizedText.Raw` by name. It keys off the fully-qualified `SpriteBatch.DrawString` name and its `string` parameter, so it needs no runtime dependency and covers only the engine primitive - a game's own `SpriteBatch`-based text helpers stay the game's to guard.
- **Escape hatches match the existing contract.** Localize the literal (resolve a `StringId` through the catalog), use `LocalizedText.Raw("...").Resolve()` for genuinely non-localizable text (then governed by `KELOC002`), or mark the enclosing scope `[LocalizationExempt]` / `[Conditional("DEBUG")]` / `#if DEBUG` (the same `IsExempt` + active-`#if DEBUG` walk `KELOC002` uses).
- **Ships as a warning across all Render2D consumers.** Default severity is Warning so no consumer build (Hardpoint, Nullwake, SpaceGame, Ruinborne) breaks on day one; a game raises it to error in `.editorconfig` (`dotnet_diagnostic.KELOC003.severity = error`) once it has cleaned its own `DrawString` literals.
- **Showcase cleaned as the worked example.** The demo captions in `Room2D` / `RoomInput` / `RoomMiniGame` (engine-feature labels, "CATCHER", "GAME OVER", the controls hint) are developer-facing chrome, so their draw methods gain `[LocalizationExempt]` with a note, the same way `RoomGui` already marks its `LocalizedText.Raw` demo screens. The Showcase builds KELOC-clean again and now demonstrates the `KELOC003` escape hatch.
- **Tests.** Nine new `KELOC003_*` cases in `LocalizationAnalyzerTests` (fires on both `DrawString` overloads; stays silent on interpolation, variables, verbatim literals, numeric/letter-free literals, single-character glyphs, `[LocalizationExempt]` scopes, and an active `#if DEBUG` region), with a `KhaozEngine.Render2D.SpriteBatch` stub added to `AnalyzerHarness`.
- Docs: `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` gains a "low-level `SpriteBatch.DrawString` sink" subsection under the localization-enforcement contract (the three fixes, the default severity, and the opt-in knob); the analyzer's own `README.md`, the `README.md` package-table row, and the `CLAUDE.md` layering note all list `KELOC003`.

## 10.2.0

Two verified follow-ups to the 10.0.0 NetId widening: a latent 64-bit despawn truncation fixed, and the engine wire-format generation now enforced unconditionally at connect (was opt-in). One minor bump for the whole batch (one version per worktree, per the repo's release rules), classified minor because the handshake change is additive at the API level (a new `WireGenerationAuthenticator`, nothing removed, the consumer `ProtocolVersion` opt-in preserved).

- **Full-snapshot despawn no longer truncates a 64-bit `NetId` (latent since 10.0.0).** `ClientReplicationView`'s full-state despawn loop iterated the gone list as `int`, so an id past 2^31 leaving the snapshot truncated on the way out: it either threw `KeyNotFoundException` out of the apply (killing the session, mislabeled "client out of date"), or, if the truncated value collided with another tracked id, silently despawned the WRONG entity while the departed one ghosted forever. Unreachable today (single-node ids are small) but it defeated the widening on that path. Fixed to `long`. The delta despawn path was already correct. Added despawn-path boundary tests (0 / `int.MaxValue` / > 2^32 / high-node-bits) plus the collision case (ids `5` and `Pack(1, 5)` both tracked, `Pack(1, 5)` leaves, entity `5` survives), which the shipped `NetIdWireBoundaryTests` never covered (they only ever applied one snapshot).
- **Engine wire generation enforced unconditionally at connect (was opt-in).** `MoveProtocol.WireProtocolVersion` is now folded into EVERY client's Hello (`WorldClient` always wraps its connect token, even with no consumer `ProtocolVersion`), and `WorldServer` / `ShardedWorldServer` always install a new **`WireGenerationAuthenticator`** that rejects a wire-generation mismatch, or a peer that presents none (a pre-10.2.0 / 9.x client), cleanly as `DisconnectReason.IncompatibleVersion`. Before this the wire gate was opt-in (a consumer had to fold `;wire{N}` into `WorldClientConfig.ProtocolVersion`), so an UNCONFIGURED 9.x/10.0 pairing misparsed instead of rejecting: a 9.x client reading the 10.0 12-byte per-client header as 8 bytes took the `ackSeq` bytes as the entity count, and `ackSeq 0` decoded as a valid EMPTY snapshot, a silent empty world with no disconnect. The consumer `ProtocolVersion` game-version gate is unchanged and now rides as an inner layer ON TOP of the automatic wire gate (a `VersionCheckingAuthenticator` composed inside the wire gate). Folding `;wire{N}` into it is no longer required. Added skew tests for the unconfigured pairing both directions, proving a clean `IncompatibleVersion` disconnect rather than a misparse.
  - **Behaviour / compatibility note.** All peers must now run the same engine wire generation: a matched client + server of this build interoperate exactly as before, but a wire-skewed or version-less peer is now rejected at connect where before it was admitted and left to misparse. Mixed-engine-version play was never supported (that is the whole point of the generation gate), so this converts a silent misparse into a clean rejection. A bare `NetClient` driven straight into a `WorldServer` / `ShardedWorldServer` (bypassing `WorldClient`) must now present the wire layer via `ProtocolHandshake.BuildClientToken(MoveProtocol.WireProtocolVersion, consumerVersion, innerToken)`. The engine test suite's raw-client helpers were migrated accordingly.
- **`NetIdAllocator.Next()` counter-exhaustion now has a test.** Construct at `startCounter: MaxCounter`: the first `Next()` hands out the final id, the next throws rather than wrapping into another node's id space.
- **`CellPersistence` restore high-water comment.** Left a note at the single-max-over-all-restored-ids that it needs a PER-NODE max when multi-node lands: a foreign-node id sorts numerically above a local one yet `EnsureNextAtLeast` ignores it (its node bits are not this node's), so one max across all nodes would leave node 0's counter unadvanced.

New public API (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`): `WireGenerationAuthenticator` (+ static `WireGenerationAuthenticator.Install`), `ProtocolHandshake.BuildClientToken`, `ProtocolHandshake.WireGenerationLabel`.

## 10.1.1

Release build is warning-clean again: cleaned up the 5 pre-existing warnings the 10.0.0 NetId merge left behind (4 ambiguous-cref doc comments + 1 nullable dereference). Doc-comment / null-guard only, no public API or behaviour change.

- **Ambiguous `<see cref>` doc comments disambiguated (CS0419).** The three `SnapshotWriter.WriteFiltered` references (`ReplicationChannels`, `SnapshotWriter`, `WorldServer`) and the `SpriteBatch.DrawRounded` reference in `NameplateRenderer` now qualify their parameter lists so each resolves to a single overload (the AoI `WriteFiltered(World, ReplicationRegistry, IReadOnlySet{long}, ReplicationChannels, long?)` and the single-colour `DrawRounded(Texture2D, Vector4, Color, float, float, float, float)`). `ReplicationChannels` imports only `System`, so its cref fully-qualifies `World` / `IReadOnlySet`.
- **`NameplateRenderer.Draw` nullable dereference guarded (CS8602).** The bar loop guards `plate.Bars` with an `is { } bars` pattern instead of indexing a possibly-null list. Identical output: a null or empty bar list already drew nothing.

## 10.1.0

`PopupPanel` (`KhaozEngine.Gui`) - the one player-facing Gui widget 9.34.0 left on raw strings - now takes `LocalizedText`, closing the last localization gap: its title / footer-button text and `PopupRow` content rows were drawn straight through `TextLayout` / routed via `LocalizedText.Raw` internally, so a consumer could write `popup.Title = "Start game?"` or `PopupRow.Stat("Name", value)` with zero warnings. Additive (minor): the new `LocalizedText` members and factories sit alongside `[Obsolete]` string shims that delegate via `LocalizedText.Raw`, so a game builds - with warnings - before migrating.

- **`PopupPanel` title + footer text are `LocalizedText`.** New `TitleContent` / `DismissContent` / `PrimaryActionContent` (`LocalizedText`, resolved each `Draw`, so a runtime locale switch re-resolves on the next frame); `DismissContent` / `PrimaryActionContent` default to `LocalizedText.Raw("Close")` / `Raw("OK")` (unchanged behaviour). The former `Title` / `DismissText` / `PrimaryActionText` `string` members become `[Obsolete]` shim properties (`get => Resolve()`, `set => LocalizedText.Raw(value)`), mirroring `Label.Text` / `Button.Label`.
- **`PopupRow` gains resolve-at-build `LocalizedText` factories.** `PopupRow.Header(LocalizedText)` and `Stat(LocalizedText, LocalizedText, Vector4)` resolve against the ambient catalog at construction (like `TooltipLine.Of`); the record still stores the resolved display strings, so rebuild the rows to reflect a locale switch. The old `Header(string)` / `Stat(string, string, Vector4)` factories are `[Obsolete]` + `[LocalizationStringSink]`, so KELOC001 flags a raw literal passed to them (property assignments are enforced by the `[Obsolete]` warning, as with `Label.Text`).
- **Showcase migrated.** `RoomGui`'s `PopupScreen` now resolves its chrome (title, buttons, headers, static note) through `StringId` (new `Popup.*` keys in `ShowcaseStrings.resx` + `ShowcaseStrings`), with `LocalizedText.Raw` (in a `[LocalizationExempt]` `LoadContent`) only for the user-entered name/difficulty values, so the analyzer-applied Showcase builds warning-clean.
- Tests: `PopupPanelLocalizedTests` (title/dismiss/primary resolve via the ambient catalog + defaults, `PopupRow.Header`/`Stat` resolve-at-build snapshot, obsolete string-shim round trip), the existing `PopupPanelTests` moved to the `LocalizedText.Raw` factories, and a `KELOC001_FiresOnMultiArgStringSink` analyzer test mirroring `PopupRow.Stat(string, string, ...)`.
- Docs: `KhaozEngine.Gui/README.md` (the localized-text sink list + the `PopupPanel` bullet) and `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` (a `PopupPanel` worked example in the localization-enforcement section).

## 10.0.0

`NetId` is now 64-bit (was a per-process 32-bit `int`), closing gap 4 of the MMO architecture review - the last decision that ossified with every shipped save and wire byte. **This is a wire- AND save-breaking change, so it is a MAJOR bump gated on the ProtocolVersion handshake:** a 10.0.0 peer and a pre-10.0.0 peer speak incompatible protocols and MUST reject each other cleanly at connect (see the wire-version gate below), and a 9.x save is brought forward by the engine's first real cell-blob migration. The old id was a raw `++counter` that wrapped after 2^31 spawns under loot-drop churn and made two processes collide on sight; the width is the hard prerequisite for any future multi-node topology.

**The decision (recorded here as the design call, not just the diff):** widen to 64-bit under a documented node-prefix allocation scheme - the high 16 bits are a node/allocator id (0 for today's single-process servers), the low 48 bits a per-node monotonic counter. Single-process behaviour is unchanged (node 0, so ids are still 1, 2, 3, …); a future multi-process layer gets collision-free allocation for free, and recycling becomes unnecessary (2^48 ids per node outlive any server). Plain 64-bit with no reservation was considered and rejected: the node prefix costs nothing today (node 0 packs to the same numeric value) and is what makes the multi-node story free later, consistent with the engine's extensible-design preference.

- **`NetId.Value` is `long`** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`), with `NetId.Node` / `NetId.Counter` accessors. The wire carries it as a 64-bit value everywhere: the snapshot / delta per-entity id field (`SnapshotWriter`, `DeltaEncoding`, `AoiDeltaReplicator`, `ServerReplicator`, `ClientReplicationView`), the persist-blob id (`SnapshotBlobReader` / `SnapshotBlobWriter`), the `InterestGrid` sets, and the `MoveProtocol` per-client frame header (`[localNetId:long][ackSeq:int]`, header grown 8 -> 12 bytes). `WorldClient.TryGetComponent(long)`, `WorldClient.LocalNetId`, `EntityRenderState.Id`, and `ReplicatedCharacterAnimators`' `CharacterSample.Id` / `CharacterPose.Id` are all 64-bit.
- **New `NetIdAllocator`** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`) is the single place ids are allocated (node bits + a per-node counter), replacing the raw `++int` in `WorldServer` / `ShardedWorldServer` / the samples. `Pack` / `NodeOf` / `CounterOf` expose the packing; `Next()` / `NextValue` / `EnsureNextAtLeast(long)` drive allocation and high-water resume. The persisted high-water (`WorldMetaRecord.NextNetId`, `ICellPersistenceHost.NextNetId` / `EnsureNextNetIdAtLeast`) is now a per-node packed `long`; `WorldMetaRecord`'s JSON is forward-tolerant, so an old 32-bit value parses into the `long` unchanged.
- **Save migration (the machinery's first real engine-provided migration).** `NetIdBlobMigration.WidenV1ToV2` (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) is a `CellSnapshotMigration` that rewrites a stored 32-bit-id snapshot body (schema v1) to 64-bit (schema v2), leaving every component byte identical - only the per-entity id field grows 4 -> 8 bytes (node 0, so id 42 stays 42). The default `CellPersistenceConfig.SchemaVersion` advances to 2, and `CellPersistence` folds the engine widening into any config at schema >= 2 (new `CellPersistenceConfig.IncludeEngineMigrations`, default true, consumer migrations override an engine step), so a server on the default config brings a 9.x cell blob forward with no wiring. A malformed body throws and is quarantined as before.
- **Wire-version gate (the compatibility posture - decided loudly).** There is NO dual-format wire: 10.0.0 speaks 64-bit only. New `MoveProtocol.WireProtocolVersion` (= 2; the pre-10.0.0 32-bit line was 1) labels the incompatible generations. A consumer folds it into its `WorldClientConfig.ProtocolVersion` and rejects a mismatch in its `VersionCheckingAuthenticator` rule, so a 10.0.0 peer and a pre-10.0.0 peer disconnect cleanly at connect (`DisconnectReason.IncompatibleVersion`) instead of misparsing a 64-bit frame as 32-bit. A 10.0.0 server that has written 64-bit cell blobs cannot be downgraded (a v2 blob is `SkippedTooNew` -> quarantined on an old build, so nothing is destroyed, but it will not load).
- **Sharding under 64-bit ids:** `CellSim`'s owned index, `ShardHost`'s netId -> cell map, the AoI interest sets, and the handoff/ghost path all carry `long`; the `MigrateAck` inter-cell payload grew from a 4-byte to an 8-byte netId.
- **Consumers pin and adopt on their own schedule. Ruinborne must adopt client and server together** (the wire break is not one-sided) and gate the connect on the `ProtocolVersion` handshake so a stale client is turned away rather than admitted onto a wire it cannot parse.
- Tests: `NetIdAllocatorTests` (monotonicity, pack/unpack + node-prefix invariants, cross-node non-collision, high-water resume, ctor bounds), `NetIdWireBoundaryTests` (snapshot / delta / blob / frame-header round trips at 0, `int.MaxValue`, a value past 2^32, and a high-node-bits id), `NetIdBlobMigrationTests` (the widening + boundary ids, a truncated-body throw, and the full `CellPersistence` boot path against a committed real 9.x blob fixture `NetWorld/Fixtures/cell-v1-32bit.blob`), and `VersionHandshakeTests` gains both skew directions producing a clean `IncompatibleVersion` (not a misparse) plus a wire-version match. The existing replication / sharding / persistence suites run green under 64-bit ids.
- Docs: `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` (a NetId / `NetIdAllocator` / wire-version section), `docs/DEPENDENCY-SEAMS.md` (the id-allocation seam), `KhaozEngine.Replication/README.md` (64-bit `NetId` + `NetIdAllocator`), `KhaozEngine.NetWorld/README.md` (the frame-header width, `WireProtocolVersion`, the engine migration + `IncludeEngineMigrations`, the `long` high-water), and `KhaozEngine.Sharding/README.md` (64-bit ownership + the widened ack payload).
## 9.34.0

Compile-time localization enforcement: player-facing Gui text now takes a `LocalizedText` value type instead of a raw `string`, so a hardcoded literal at a UI sink is a compile error, with a Roslyn analyzer and an explicit `LocalizedText.Raw` escape hatch keeping the exemption honest. Additive: the old `string` Gui overloads remain (marked `[Obsolete]`, delegating to the new ones via `LocalizedText.Raw`), so a game builds - with warnings - before migrating any text.

- **New in `KhaozEngine.App`.** `StringId` (a typed localization key with NO implicit `string` conversion - authoring one is deliberate, which is what blocks bare literals), `LocalizedText` (what the sinks accept: either a localizable `StringId` + optional format args or a raw literal; implicit from `StringId`, explicit `LocalizedText.Raw(...)`; resolves lazily against the ambient catalog on every access, so a runtime locale switch re-resolves on the next draw with nothing to invalidate), `LocalizationContext.Catalog` (the ambient `IStringCatalog` a `LocalizedText` resolves against; null renders the key as a visible placeholder), and the `[LocalizationExempt]` / `[LocalizationStringSink]` marker attributes.
- **`KhaozEngine.Gui` sinks take `LocalizedText`.** The `Label` and `Button` widgets, `GuiSurface.Label` / `Button` / `StatChip`, `GuiDraw.DrawButton` (internal), and `Tooltip.Show` (+ `TooltipLine.Of`) gained `LocalizedText` overloads; the `string` overloads are `[Obsolete]` + `[LocalizationStringSink]` and delegate via `LocalizedText.Raw`, so behaviour is unchanged. `Gui` now references `App` (acyclic). `IconButton` is unchanged - its string is an icon-atlas key, not player text.
- **New package `KhaozEngine.Localization.Analyzers`** (a `netstandard2.0` Roslyn analyzer). `KELOC001` flags a raw string passed to any `[LocalizationStringSink]` member; `KELOC002` flags `LocalizedText.Raw(...)` outside `[LocalizationExempt]` scopes and DEBUG-conditional code (`[Conditional("DEBUG")]` member/type or an active `#if DEBUG` region). Both ship as warnings; a repo raises either to error in `.editorconfig`. It flows to consumers as a packed dependency (`include="All"`) of the `Game2D` / `Game3D` umbrellas, applied in the consumer's build.
- **Showcase migrated as the worked example.** `KhaozEngine.Showcase` gains `ShowcaseStrings.resx` + hand-authored `StringId` constants wired through `LocalizationContext.Catalog`, with `LocalizedText.Raw` + scoped `[LocalizationExempt]` for the dynamic `%` readout and the immediate-mode demo chrome. It references the analyzer, so KELOC is enforced on real code in-repo.
- **Tests.** `StringIdTests`, `LocalizedTextTests` (raw vs id, format args, no-catalog placeholder, `default` -> "", locale-switch re-resolve), `LocalizationContextTests`, `LocalizationAttributesTests`, Gui widget resolve-at-draw tests, `ShowcaseStringsTests` (every `StringId` constant has a resx entry), and the new `KhaozEngine.Localization.Analyzers.Tests` project (KELOC001/002 fire, and stay silent under exempt type/method/assembly, `[Conditional("DEBUG")]`, and an active `#if DEBUG` region).
- **Docs.** The `README.md` package catalog (App + Gui rows, new analyzer row, umbrella note), `KhaozEngine.App/README.md` + `KhaozEngine.Gui/README.md`, a "Compile-time localization enforcement" adoption section in `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md`, the localization package edges in `docs/DEPENDENCY-SEAMS.md`, and a `.resx` -> `StringId` source-generator follow-up on `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## 9.33.0

The cell persistence blob (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) gains a migration path, a non-throwing quarantining restore, unknown-extension retention, and a surfaced diagnostics event, closing gap 3 of the MMO architecture review (the last "wipe or corrupt the world at rest" hazard). Before this, a component-layout change forced a choice between wiping the world (bump `SchemaVersion` so old blobs are skipped) or corrupting it (do not bump), a corrupt key crash-looped the server on every boot, and a registry regression silently stripped unknown components and re-persisted the loss. Additive: the constructor, the wire format, and existing current-version restores are unchanged (a current-`SchemaVersion` blob still restores byte-identically), so a save with no migrations registered behaves exactly as before.

- **Migration hooks (deliverable 1).** `CellPersistenceConfig.RegisterMigration(fromVersion, migrate)` registers a `CellSnapshotMigration` (`byte[] snapshotBody -> byte[]`) applied in order on load when the stored version is older than `SchemaVersion`, before restore. The chain is validated at `CellPersistence` construction (contiguous, no gaps, no step at or beyond `SchemaVersion`), mirroring `KhaozEngine.Persistence.MigrationChain` semantics without adding a package edge. A blob older than the earliest migration is skipped with a `SkippedTooOld` event (never misread); a blob newer than this build is skipped with `SkippedTooNew`. Author migrations with the new `SnapshotBlobReader` / `SnapshotBlobWriter` (below), which walk `[count][per entity: netId + component frames]` so a consumer maps / drops / transforms per-component payloads without hand-parsing. Engine-owned built-in layout changes ship engine-provided migrations; consumer extension changes ship consumer migrations.
- **Non-throwing quarantining restore (deliverable 2).** Restore now runs through `CellSim.TryRestoreOwned` (via the new `ICellPersistenceHost.TryRestoreCell`), which uses `TryApply` semantics and rolls back a partial apply. A blob that fails to decode (bad header, corrupt frame, a migration threw, restore rejected it) is QUARANTINED, not thrown: the cell starts fresh, the original bytes are copied to `quarantine:cell:{x}:{y}` (nothing destroyed), and the failure is surfaced as `QuarantinedCorrupt`. A poisoned key can no longer crash-loop the server on every boot.
- **Unknown-extension retention (deliverable 3).** An extension frame whose id the current registry does not know is now retained per-entity in the cell's persistence bookkeeping and re-emitted verbatim on the next save (retain-and-rewrite), so a temporary registry regression (a rollback, a build missing a registration) no longer permanently strips data at rest. Under the full registry the component reappears intact. Documented limitation: a retained frame does not follow a cell handoff during a regression (there is no live component to migrate), so retention protects the restart load/save cycle, which is the stated goal.
- **Surfaced diagnostics (deliverable 4).** New `CellPersistence.Issue` (`event Action<CellPersistenceIssue>`), raised on the server thread inside the load-apply drain, reports `Migrated` (from -> to), `SkippedTooOld`, `SkippedTooNew`, `QuarantinedCorrupt` (with the decode error), and `RetainedUnknownExtensions` (with the count). Consumers (Ruinborne ops) can SEE what was silent before.
- **New public API (additive):** `KhaozEngine.Replication`: `SnapshotBlobReader` (+ `SnapshotBlobEntity` / `SnapshotBlobComponent`), `SnapshotBlobWriter`, `RetainedComponent`, `ClientReplicationView.TryApplyRetainingUnknown`, and a `SnapshotWriter.WriteFiltered` overload taking a per-netId retained-frames provider. `KhaozEngine.Sharding`: `CellSim.TryRestoreOwned` returning `CellRestoreResult` (`RestoreOwned` kept, now non-throwing, delegating to it). `KhaozEngine.NetWorld`: `CellSnapshotMigration`, `CellPersistenceConfig.RegisterMigration` + `QuarantineKeyPrefix`, `CellPersistenceIssue` / `CellPersistenceIssueKind`, `CellPersistence.Issue`, and `ICellPersistenceHost.TryRestoreCell` (a default interface method, so existing implementers are unaffected).
- **A migrated blob is rewritten once** with the current header on the next dirty pass, upgrading the on-disk schema version so a later boot does not re-migrate. A clean or retention-only current-version restore seeds the dirty baseline so an unchanged cell is not re-saved.
- Tests: `SnapshotBlobTests` (reader/writer byte-identical round trip, built-in-length resolver, corrupt-frame guard), `ClientReplicationViewRetentionTests` (retain unknown extension, apply known, unknown built-in fails non-throwing, re-emit overload), `CellSimRetentionTests` (unknown extension survives a reduced-registry round trip and reappears under the full registry, corrupt snapshot rolls back), `CellPersistenceConfigTests` (register/duplicate/null), and `CellPersistenceMigrationTests` (single-step migrate + restore, two-step chain composes, chain gap throws at construction, corrupt / migration-threw / decode-failure quarantine with the bytes preserved and the server still ticking, too-old / too-new skip, current-version byte-identical restore, retained-unknown and migrated events surfaced).
- Docs: the `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` cell-persistence section (the 9.28.0 "documented, not built" note now points at the built machinery + a new migration / quarantine / retention / events subsection), `KhaozEngine.NetWorld/README.md` + `KhaozEngine.Replication/README.md` + `KhaozEngine.Sharding/README.md`, the `README.md` package catalog rows, and the `docs/DEPENDENCY-SEAMS.md` per-cell-persistence seam.

## 9.32.1

Fixes a data-loss race in `WorldPersistence` (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) where a periodic save or a quick leave firing while a load-on-join was still in flight overwrote the stored record with default-spawn state - erasing the durable per-player game blob 9.32.0 added (position had the same race, but a null blob made it destructive). Ruinborne, running the async `SqlServerWorldStore` in the cloud, was the exposure: the four existing game-state tests used a synchronous `InMemoryWorldStore`, so the in-flight window never opened. `WorldPersistence` now guards each account across its load-on-join exactly as `CellPersistence` already did for cells. Bug-fix + behaviour hardening; no API change beyond the additive `OnStoreError` event.

- **In-flight load guard (the fix).** An account with an outstanding load-on-join is tracked from `OnPlayerJoined` until the loaded record is applied on the server thread (the `DrainApplyQueue` apply, not mere task completion), or dropped immediately if the load found no saved record. Both the periodic dirty pass (`SaveDirtyPass`) and save-on-leave (`OnPlayerLeaving`) skip a guarded account, so a save landing mid-load can no longer capture the default spawn + a null blob and clobber the stored record. Skipping the leave-save is correct: the stored record was never applied, so it - not the pre-restore live state - is the truth worth keeping. A faulted load deliberately leaves the guard set so the intact stored record stays protected (a later rejoin retries the load). Mirrors `CellPersistence.loadsInFlight`.
- **New public API (additive): `WorldPersistence.OnStoreError`** (`event Action<Exception>`). `Update` now prunes *faulted and canceled* tracked tasks too, not only `RanToCompletion` - a store outage no longer grows the pending list unbounded until `FlushAsync` - and surfaces each failure through this hook (raised on the server thread, outside the pending lock). The failed save's state stays dirty and retries on the next pass.
- **`CaptureGameState` erase contract documented.** Returning null / empty means "no game state" and is *destructive*: after a save has written bytes it marks the record dirty and ERASES the stored blob. It is not a "not loaded yet" signal - a capture hook that returns null before its live object is ready wipes the player's progression. Spelled out in the `PlayerGameStateCapture` xmldoc and the USING guide, and locked by a new test.
- **Known remaining edge (documented, not fixed).** On an async store, store operations for the same account are not ordered across a rapid leave/rejoin that overlaps an in-flight load-on-join, so a rejoin can briefly apply pre-leave state, which the next periodic save reconciles. It is documented at the seam rather than fixed: a per-account operation chain (or a refcount guard) was judged not cheap enough to be worth the added complexity and its own trade-offs (a refcount, unlike this presence guard, would not recover saving after a faulted load even on a clean rejoin).
- Tests: `WorldPersistenceLoadRaceTests` (new) drives the in-flight window with a new `GatedWorldStore` async double - a periodic save mid-load does not write, a join-then-instant-leave mid-load keeps the stored blob and it survives to the next rejoin, a null load clears the guard so later saves proceed, capture returning null-after-bytes erases the blob, and a faulted save is pruned and surfaced through `OnStoreError`; `WorldPersistenceTests` gains the same in-flight-clobber assertion driven through the real `WorldServer` over `LoopbackTransport`.
- Docs: `WorldPersistence` / `PlayerGameStateCapture` xmldoc, `KhaozEngine.NetWorld/README.md`, and the `WorldPersistence` section of `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` gain the in-flight guard, the destructive-null contract, `OnStoreError`, and the rejoin-ordering limitation.

## 9.32.0

`WorldPersistence` (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) can now carry a game-owned durable per-player blob (XP, skills, inventory, quest log) beside the position it already persists, riding the SAME record, dirty-tracking, interval save, flush-on-drain and load-on-join thread-marshalling - gap 7 of the MMO arch review. A game supplies two hooks on `WorldPersistenceConfig`; the engine keeps the payload opaque (it never deserializes it), mirroring the game-message seam, so a game no longer has to re-implement the whole load-on-join / save-on-leave / periodic-dirty / thread-marshalling machinery over its own `IWorldStore` keyspace. Purely additive: the constructor and existing position-only behaviour are unchanged, and old saves (no blob) decode fine.

- **New public API (additive):** `WorldPersistenceConfig.CaptureGameState` (a `PlayerGameStateCapture` delegate) and `WorldPersistenceConfig.ApplyGameState` (a `PlayerGameStateApply` delegate), the `PlayerPersistenceContext` readonly struct (`Slot` + `AccountId`) passed to both, and a second `PlayerRecord.From(in PlayerMoveState, byte[]? game)` overload plus the `PlayerRecord.Game` blob field.
- **Capture runs on the server thread** at every save point (save-on-leave and the periodic dirty pass), so the hook may read the live per-player object directly by `PlayerPersistenceContext.Slot`; the returned bytes are folded into the same `PlayerRecord` as position. Return null / empty for "no game state" (position-only, encodes identically to before).
- **Apply runs on the server thread** as the load-on-join position is applied (in the `Update` / `FlushAsync` drain, never a background continuation), handing back exactly the bytes the matching capture returned. Never fired for a player with no saved blob. The `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` is valid only for the call - copy it to keep the bytes.
- **One record, whole-record dirty comparison.** The blob lives in the existing `player:{accountId}` record (base64 in the JSON, forward-tolerant) rather than a second key, so position and the game blob save atomically and a change to *either* marks the record dirty and re-saves. A second key would have doubled the store round-trips and needed its own load/flush/dirty tracking.
- **Migration is game-side and opaque to the engine.** Because the engine never deserializes the blob, schema evolution happens inside the game's apply hook: deserialize, run a `KhaozEngine.Persistence.MigrationChain` (or any game scheme), then attach. A schema bump therefore never corrupts a save. The engine's own `PlayerRecord` position fields stay forward-tolerant as before.
- **Account-keyed, so unaffected by cell handoff.** The record is keyed by account, and `ShardedWorldServer` handoff relocates the entity between cells with a stable netId without raising leave/join - so the durable blob is untouched by handoff, distinct from registered components (which migrate cell-to-cell with the entity).
- Tests: `WorldPersistenceGameStateTests` - a blob round-trips through join -> dirty save -> leave -> rejoin, survives a simulated restart via an enumerable `InMemoryWorldStore`, a schema bump migrates an old blob through a game-side `MigrationChain` in the apply hook, and position and the game blob each independently mark the record dirty (and each is preserved when only the other changes).
- Docs: `KhaozEngine.NetWorld/README.md` + the README package-catalog row gain the game-state seam, and `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` its `WorldPersistence` section a durable-per-player-state subsection with the migration recipe.

## 9.31.0

`ShardHost.TryGetOwner` and `CellSim.TryGetOwned` (`KhaozEngine.Sharding`) now resolve entity ownership in O(1) off a maintained netId -> (cell, entity) index instead of a linear `World.ForEach` across every cell - gap 6 of the MMO arch review and the top server-CPU item. These are called per player and (per the documented OnBeforeTick NPC-brain pattern) per NPC per tick from several sites in `ShardedWorldServer.Tick`, so the old scan made a tick O(population x total entities) - quadratic in NPC count, the wall the population hits first. The lookup is now a dictionary hit. Additive and internal-only: no wire change, and existing `SpawnAt` + `TryGetOwner` / `TryGetOwned` call sites compile and behave unchanged.

- **The index has two halves kept in lockstep.** Each `CellSim` maintains a `netId -> owned entity` map (present, alive, not a `Ghost`, not `Migrating`), and `ShardHost` maintains a `netId -> owning cell` map projected from it via internal register/unregister hooks wired when the cell is created - so restore, adopt, spawn and the migrate-freeze all propagate to the host map with no extra bookkeeping. Maintained ONLY at the ownership choke points: the spawn path, `AdoptFromMigrate`, `RestoreOwned`, `ReleaseMigrating`, and the migrate-freeze in `ProcessHandoffs` (an entity is dropped from the owned index the moment it is frozen, preserving the "owned = not Ghost, not Migrating" semantics). Ghosts never enter the owned index, so a ghost of netId N in cell B never makes `TryGetOwner` return B while A still owns N. The steady-state tick mutates the index, never rebuilds it, so it adds no per-tick allocation.
- **New public API (additive):** `ShardHost.SpawnOwned(worldX, worldY, netId, out cell)` (spawn + assign `NetId` + register in one eager step), and `CellSim.RegisterOwned(netId, entity)` / `CellSim.UnregisterOwned(netId)` for consumers that spawn/despawn owned entities through the raw `World`.
- **Non-breaking by design.** The pre-index `World.ForEach` scan is kept BEHIND the index as `TryGetOwned`'s self-healing miss-fallback: a lookup miss scans once and caches the hit (so the pre-index raw spawn idiom `SpawnAt` + `World.Set(new NetId(..))` without a register still resolves), and a stale index entry (an out-of-band despawn, or the entity became a ghost / started migrating) is reaped on lookup. There is one source of truth - the index - with the scan only as its fallback + oracle.
- **`OwnerCount` stays an independent from-scratch scan on purpose:** it is the exactly-once handoff oracle (asserting exactly one owner at every `ProcessHandoffs` boundary), so it must be able to observe a duplicate (2) or loss (0) that a structurally-single-valued index never could.
- **Shipping consumers routed through the eager path** so the server pays no scan: `ShardedWorldServer` (`SpawnEntity`, player-join spawn, player-leave despawn) and the `MmoServerSample`.
- Tests: `ShardHostOwnerIndexTests` - the index equals a from-scratch scan after every tick across a 40-entity cross-cell migration stress (with the exactly-once invariant re-asserted each tick), a ghost never resolves as an owner, a despawn drops the netId from both index halves, the raw spawn idiom still resolves via the fallback, and the hot `TryGetOwner` path allocates zero bytes.
- Bench: `OwnerLookupBenchmark` (a new ownership-lookup axis in `KhaozEngine.Benchmarks`) times `TryGetOwner` against a naive linear owner-scan across a sweep of entity counts - the index cost stays flat while the scan grows linearly.
- Docs: `KhaozEngine.Sharding/README.md` gains the ownership-index API and `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` notes the O(1) lookup and `SpawnOwned` on the NPC-brain pattern.

## 9.30.0

`PrimitiveRenderer` (`KhaozEngine.Render2D`) can now stroke a PARTIAL ring - `DrawArc` for a general arc outline and `DrawRadialProgress` for a 0..1 fill-fraction ring (countdown / cooldown / progress dials, the immediate ask being a Nullwake ore-respawn countdown). This fills the gap where `DrawCircle` / `DrawRing` only strokes a FULL circle and `DrawFilledSector` / `DrawFilledArcBand` only FILL a wedge - nothing strokes a partial arc. Purely additive; no existing API or behaviour changed.

- **`PrimitiveRenderer.DrawArc(batch, center, radius, thickness, startAngleRadians, sweepAngleRadians, color, segments = 64)`** (`KhaozEngine.Render2D`). Strokes an arc outline as `thickness`-width line segments the same way `DrawCircle` strokes a full circle (each a rotated quad via `DrawLine`). Angles are radians in screen space (+Y down, so a positive sweep goes clockwise); `-PI/2` is 12 o'clock. The sweep is arbitrary - it may exceed 2PI or be negative for the other direction - and the number of segments actually drawn scales with the arc's fraction of a full turn (`ceil(segments * |sweep| / 2PI)`, floored at 1) so a thin sweep stays smooth instead of spending the whole `segments` budget on it. No-op (draws nothing, never throws) when radius, thickness, or segments is non-positive.
- **`PrimitiveRenderer.DrawRadialProgress(batch, center, radius, thickness, fraction, color, segments = 64, startAngleRadians = -PI/2, clockwise = true)`** (`KhaozEngine.Render2D`). Convenience over `DrawArc`: strokes `clamp(fraction, 0, 1)` of a full ring from 12 o'clock, clockwise by default - `0` draws nothing, `1` a full ring. Internally computes `sweep = clamp(fraction,0,1) * 2PI` (negated when `clockwise` is false) and delegates to `DrawArc`. For a countdown ring feed the remaining fraction.
- **Pure helpers `ArcSegments(segments, sweep)` and `RadialProgressSweep(fraction, clockwise)`** (`KhaozEngine.Render2D`), extracted `static` for headless tests exactly like the existing `RingSegments` / `SectorSegments` / `ComputeProgressBarLayout`.
- Docs: `KhaozEngine.Render2D/README.md` gains a `PrimitiveRenderer` entry (the primitive family + the new arc / radial-progress helpers), and `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` its Render2D section a radial-progress note.
- Tests: `PrimitiveArcTests` - fraction clamp to [0,1], clockwise sign flip, segment-count scaling with the sweep fraction, plus the floor-at-1 / abs-of-sweep / zero-on-non-positive-segments edges.

## 9.29.0

`ServerReplicator` - the documented whole-world delta client-serving path (`docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md` points consumers at it "for bandwidth") - now honours `ReplicationChannels`, closing the last channel-blind serving path left by 9.28.0. Before this it looped every registered codec in `Capture` with no channel gate and had no `ownerNetId` in `WriteFor`, so a consumer serving clients through a flagged registry would have put `Persist`/`Migrate`-only server state AND every player's `OwnerOnly` components on the wire to everyone. No shipped path drove it (only `CellSim.Replicator`, exercised by tests), so this was a latent footgun rather than a live leak, but the path is public and recommended, so it is brought to full parity with `SnapshotWriter` / `AoiDeltaReplicator` rather than fenced off. Additive: `Capture(world)` keeps its signature and `WriteFor` gains an optional `ownerNetId`, so a registry using only `Default` is byte-identical and existing `WriteFor(slot)` calls compile unchanged.

- **`ServerReplicator.Capture` captures only the `Replicate` channel** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`). A `Persist`- or `Migrate`-only server component is no longer snapshotted into the shared history, so it can never reach a client through this path. `OwnerOnly` components ARE captured (keyed under their entity) because a single shared capture serves every client; they are scoped per client at write time.
- **`ServerReplicator.WriteFor(slot, ownerNetId = null)`** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`). The shared capture is projected per client before diffing: an `OwnerOnly` component is emitted only for the entity whose net id equals `ownerNetId` (this slot's own player), and to nobody when it is null. Both the acked baseline and the current snapshot are projected under the SAME owner scope, so the delta never leaks another player's owner-only bytes - not even as a spurious component removal - and stays consistent across baseline advances. Pass a stable owner net id per slot (a player's fixed session net id). A registry with no `OwnerOnly` component skips projection entirely (no allocation, wire byte-identical to before).
- **Consumer-facing `Persist`-without-`Migrate` footgun docs** (`KhaozEngine.Replication/README.md`, `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md`). A component registered `Persist` but not `Migrate` survives a server restart yet is dropped the instant its entity crosses a cell boundary (handoff captures only the `Migrate` channel), so on a seamless sharded world it silently vanishes mid-session. This was only noted in the `ShardHost.ProcessHandoffs` xmldoc, so it is now called out where consumers actually pick channels.
- Tests: the 9.28.0 channel matrix extended to `ServerReplicator` - `OwnerOnly` reaches only the owner (and nobody with no owner), server-only / `Persist`-only / `Migrate`-only components never on its wire, a change to another player's `OwnerOnly` produces zero churn in an observer's delta (the baseline-projection guard, asserted on the decoded delta header), and a defaults registry is owner-invariant (byte-identical `WriteFor` with and without an owner).

## 9.28.1

Fixes a remotely-triggerable server crash (DoS) in the 9.27.0 client->server game-message decode: any joined client could take down the entire host - every session, not just its own connection - with a single malformed 5-byte frame.

- **`MoveProtocol.TryDecodeGameMessage` underflow guard** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`). A pad-flagged game-message frame with no payload left after the pad byte is stripped (`end < GameMessageHeader`, i.e. a 5-byte `[0xC5][0xB0][kind][flags-with-pad-bit]` frame) sliced a NEGATIVE-length payload and threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
