That throw propagated out of `WorldServer.HandleData` / `ShardedWorldServer.HandleData`, which run inside the `Poll` dequeue loop, so it crashed the whole host rather than flagging one connection. The decode now returns false for such a frame, so it falls through to the move decode and is flagged `SuspiciousReason.MalformedPacket` via `OnSuspiciousActivity` exactly like any other garbage packet - never thrown. This restores the 9.27.0 "oversize/garbage flagged, never thrown" contract, which never covered this length. No API or wire change; a well-formed game message (the encoder never emits a payload-less pad-flagged frame) is byte-identical.
- **Doc correction (version skew).** The 9.27.0 note claiming a game-message frame "cannot be misparsed as a move by an old server (the 18-byte guard)" was wrong and is corrected here and in `KhaozEngine.NetWorld/README.md` + `docs/USING-KHAOZENGINE.md`: only an exactly-18-byte frame is guarded, and the encoder never emits one, so a game message whose total length is >= 18 (a payload of >= 13 bytes) decodes as a spurious finite move on a server that predates the feature. The `WorldClientConfig.ProtocolVersion` handshake, not the framing, is what protects an old server.
- Tests: the malformed-frame case (5-byte pad-flagged empty, header-length pad-flagged, and below-header truncations) driven through the real `WorldServer` and `ShardedWorldServer` `HandleData`/`Poll` over `LoopbackTransport`, asserting the server does NOT throw and the frame is flagged `MalformedPacket` - the coverage the 36 existing game-message tests never exercised (none fed a malformed frame through `HandleData`).

## 9.28.0

Per-registration replication channels in `KhaozEngine.Replication`, so one registry no longer forces persisted == replicated == migrated. `ReplicationRegistry.Register<T>` gains an optional `ReplicationChannels` flag (`Replicate` = client area-of-interest serving + border ghosts, `Persist` = cell blob, `Migrate` = cell handoff, plus `OwnerOnly` as a `Replicate` modifier). Default is `Replicate | Persist | Migrate` (the pre-9.28.0 behaviour), so every existing registration and built-in is unchanged and the wire stays byte-identical for them. This unblocks two MMO state shapes the old coupling made impossible: a mob's server-only aggro / loot / quest state (`Persist | Migrate`, no `Replicate`) survives cell handoff and a restart but never reaches a client, and a player's private inventory / exact HP (`Default | OwnerOnly`) reaches only its own client, never another observer in area-of-interest (closing a map-hack surface). Additive; the movement wire and existing ctors are unchanged.

- **`ReplicationChannels` `[Flags]` enum + `Register<T>` `channels` parameter** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`). Each of the four consumers of a component's bytes now serves exactly one channel and includes a component only if it declared that channel. `SnapshotWriter.Write` / `WriteFiltered` and `AoiDeltaReplicator.WriteFor` take the serving channel + an optional `ownerNetId` (both default to `Replicate` / no owner, so existing calls compile unchanged). The flags gate the **server (write) side** only - the client read side decodes whatever is on the wire, so channel flags on a client-built registry are ignored.
- **Owner-only visibility** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`). On the `Replicate` channel an `OwnerOnly` component is written only for the entity whose `NetId` equals the receiving client's own player net id. The servers thread that id automatically (`WorldServer` / `ShardedWorldServer` / `MmoServer` for both the full-snapshot and AoI-delta serve paths). Because the per-slot delta baseline stores exactly what THAT slot was sent, owner-only visibility falls out of the delta diff with no extra baseline bookkeeping - an observer's snapshot AND delta both lack another player's owner-only component, including across a cell handoff.
- **Channel routing at each sharding consumer** (`KhaozEngine.Sharding`). `CellSim.SnapshotOwned` captures the `Persist` channel, `ShardHost.ProcessHandoffs` captures `Migrate`, and `ShardHost.SyncGhosts` mirrors `Replicate` with no owner (documented rule: a ghost is a read-only mirror served to OTHER cells' clients, so `Persist`/`Migrate`-only server state and `OwnerOnly` private state are never ghosted; nothing in the ghost path reads a non-`Replicate` component). `ShardHost.SnapshotForClient` serves `Replicate` scoped to the client's own player.
- **Protocol safety.** A built-in id (`< FirstExtensionTypeId`) must keep `Default` - its exact unframed encoding is the core protocol - so `Register` throws on any non-default channel set below the floor; `OwnerOnly` without `Replicate` also throws. Built-in ids `1..15` keep all channels and their byte-identical wire.
- **Cell-blob compatibility** (documented, not built). Changing a component's channels changes what future saves write into a cell's persist blob; an old blob restored through a registry whose extension set shrank already skips unknown ids (the versioned `CellPersistence` header + length-prefixed extension framing). Real cell-blob schema migration (rewriting old blobs) remains a separate upcoming item; bump `CellPersistenceConfig.SchemaVersion` on a breaking layout change so old saves are skipped, not misread.
- **`MmoServerSample`.** The `Creature` NPC now carries a hidden `AggroCounter` (`Persist | Migrate`, never replicated) and each player carries an `OwnerOnly` `PrivateStats` (exact HP), demonstrating both shapes end to end.
- Tests: a matrix of each flag through each path (snapshot, delta, ghost, handoff, persist round-trip), the `OwnerOnly` no-leak guarantee on snapshot + delta including across a real cell handoff, a `Persist`-only component that survives restart but never replicates, a `Migrate`-only component that survives handoff but neither persists nor replicates, byte-identical wire for a defaults registry, and the registry guards.

## 9.27.0

Generic game-message seam in `KhaozEngine.NetWorld`, so a game (attack, interaction, pick-up, chat, inventory transaction) is no longer forced into a side channel around the movement protocol. Client->server: `WorldClient.SendGameMessage(ushort kind, ReadOnlySpan<byte> payload, NetChannelReliability reliability)` and an `OnGameMessage(int slot, ushort kind, ReadOnlySpan<byte> payload)` event on BOTH `WorldServer` and `ShardedWorldServer`, fired on the host thread during `Poll`. Server->client: a new `ServerFrameKind.GameMessage`, plus `SendGameMessageTo(slot, kind, payload, reliability)` and `BroadcastGameMessage(kind, payload, reliability)` on both servers, surfaced on the client as `WorldClient.GameMessageReceived(kind, payload)`. Payloads are opaque bytes: the engine frames, demuxes, rate-limits and size-caps them but never deserializes them (quest/inventory/chat systems stay game-side). Additive; the movement wire and existing ctors are unchanged.

- **Client->server game messages** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`). `WorldClient.SendGameMessage` frames a message in the existing `0xC5` control-marker family with its own sub-marker (`MoveProtocol.EncodeGameMessage` / `TryDecodeGameMessage`), demuxed on the server ahead of the move. The framing can never alias the 2 / 6 / 18 byte control / ack / move shapes: the decode rejects length 18 outright (always a move) and the encoder never emits an 18-byte frame (it pads a would-be-18 frame to 19 and flags it), so a real move is never stolen and a game message never falls through to the move decode. Demux order is documented in `MoveProtocol`.
- **Server->client game messages** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`). New `MoveProtocol.ServerFrameKind.GameMessage` carrying `[ushort kind][payload]` (`EncodeGameMessageBody` / `TryDecodeGameMessageBody`). An older client's frame demux ignores an unknown `ServerFrameKind`, so server->client is version-skew-safe downstream (covered by a test).
- **Hostile-input hardening** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`). The per-connection `AntiCheat` rate limiter runs in front of game messages (they share the move flood budget), and a payload over the new `WorldServerConfig.MaxGameMessageBytes` / `ShardedWorldServerConfig.MaxGameMessageBytes` (default 1024) is dropped and flagged `SuspiciousReason.OversizedMessage` (new) via `OnSuspiciousActivity` - never thrown. No engine-side deserialization of the opaque payload.
- **Reliability semantics.** `ReliableOrdered` gives ordered exactly-once delivery at the transport (a command consumer needs no seq of its own); `UnreliableSequenced` is available for lossy state pings. Both directions forward the caller's chosen channel to the transport verbatim (covered by a test).
- **Version skew.** The `WorldClientConfig.ProtocolVersion` handshake is what protects a server that predates game messages, not the framing: a game-aware client must not send a game message until the handshake confirms the peer understands it. The framing alone does NOT shield an old server - only a game-message frame SHORTER than the 18-byte move is flagged malformed there; one whose total length is >= 18 (a payload of >= 13 bytes) is misparsed as a spurious finite move. Gate adoption on the handshake. (Corrected in 9.28.1; the original claim that "the 18-byte guard" prevents an old-server misparse was wrong - only an exactly-18-byte frame is guarded, and the encoder never emits one.)
- **`MmoServerSample`.** Demonstrates the seam end to end with a chat line: `MmoProtocol.EncodeChat` (reusing `MoveProtocol.EncodeGameMessage`) -> `MmoServer.ChatReceived` / `LastChat`, demuxed ahead of the move exactly as `WorldServer.HandleData` does. Run `MmoServerSample --chat-demo`.
- Tests: headless loopback round trips both directions on both servers and both reliability modes, the rate-limit + size-cap violations flagged, an old-style client ignoring the new server frame, the kind demux not aliasing moves/controls/acks (including the padded-18 case), and slot recycle not leaking messages across occupants.

## 9.26.0

Runtime window placement: window position and monitor are now gettable and settable live, and the `DisplaySettings` snapshot round-trips the whole placement (monitor + position + size + mode + present) in one `ApplyDisplay`, so a consumer can persist and restore where its window sits across launches. 9.24.0 exposed present mode / frame cap / window mode / size on `GameApp.Display` but had no window position or monitor control; this adds it. New position accessors mirror the existing size convention (`WindowX` / `WindowY` getters + `MoveTo`, matching `WindowWidth` / `WindowHeight` + `Resize`), monitor enumeration + selection (`Monitors` / `CurrentMonitorIndex` / `MoveToMonitor`), and an `EnsureVisible` clamp that pulls a restored window back on-screen when its saved monitor is gone (unplugged / different layout). All placement math is pure and headless-tested in a new `WindowPlacement` static (which monitor / centre-on / clamp-visible), keeping the input/windowing hard rule intact: only `AppWindow` touches the Silk monitor statics. Additive; all existing APIs unchanged and the `DisplaySettings` 5-arg construction still compiles.

- **Window position + monitor on `IDisplaySettings`** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing` + `KhaozEngine.Game`). New `WindowX` / `WindowY` getters + `MoveTo(int, int)` (applied immediately when windowed, remembered as the windowed position to restore in a fullscreen mode, symmetric with `Resize`); `IReadOnlyList<MonitorInfo> Monitors` (index, name, bounds), `int CurrentMonitorIndex`, and `void MoveToMonitor(int)` (centre on that monitor when windowed, re-cover it when borderless fullscreen); `void EnsureVisible()`. All implemented on `AppWindow` and surfaced through `GameApp.Display` for free. `AppWindow` builds the `MonitorInfo` list from Silk's `Monitor.GetMonitors` (empty on headless) and stays the only class touching the windowing statics.
- **`DisplaySettings` round-trips placement** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`). The `DisplaySettings` snapshot gains `int X` / `int Y` (window top-left in virtual-desktop coordinates, defaulting to a new `PositionUnspecified` sentinel with a `HasPosition` helper), so `CurrentDisplay` captures the full placement and `ApplyDisplay` restores it. The applied order is now window mode -> resolution -> placement -> frame cap -> present; the placement step clamps the saved position on-screen before moving, so a stale position on a now-gone monitor self-corrects. Absolute position is the canonical placement (it already encodes which monitor); monitor index is a live-only enumeration convenience.
- **Pure `WindowPlacement` policy** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`). New headless-testable `WindowPlacement` static (mirrors `WindowModePlanner`): `MonitorIndexFor` (centre-containment, else greatest overlap, else nearest centre, -1 when empty), `CenterOn`, and `ClampVisible` (relocate a window whose monitor is gone onto its best / nearest monitor, pin a larger-than-monitor window to the origin so the title bar stays reachable, position only). Plus a `MonitorInfo` record (index / name / bounds). `WindowModePlanner.Compute` gains optional windowed-position params so returning to windowed restores a remembered position (default-off, unchanged for consumers that never call `MoveTo`).

## 9.25.0

Updater relaunch-race fix + a lightweight native progress window for the shim. Every Windows update applied correctly but the shim's immediate post-apply relaunch of the game crashed at startup (`0xc0000142` STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED / `0xc0000409` STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN, intermittent) while a manual launch seconds later booted fine. Root cause: on a `PublishSingleFile` self-contained bundle, Windows Defender scans the freshly-written exe and briefly holds an exclusive lock, and the shim relaunched into that mid-scan image. Fix (Part A): the applier now polls a new `IUpdaterEnvironment.CanOpenExclusively` (real impl opens with `FileShare.None`; true on non-Windows, so POSIX is a no-op) until the exe is launchable, up to a 30s ceiling, then relaunches, so it never starts the game into a scan-locked binary. Part B makes the previously-invisible shim phase visible: a tiny self-contained Win32 GDI progress window (P/Invoke only, no WinForms/WPF, no common-controls dependency, no engine GUI/GPU stack, trim/AOT-safe) shows Install (files copied / total) then Finishing ("Finishing up, checking with your security software...") during exactly that settle wait, instead of a frozen gap or a raw OS crash dialog. The window is themeable and localizable by the consumer via an optional `UpdaterUiOptions` block (title, accent/background/text colors, logo, phase strings) that `UpdateService.ApplyUpdate` serializes into `apply-update.json`; absent, the shim shows a minimal default window (or nothing off Windows). The consumer's shim stays a one-liner (`UpdaterShim.Main(args)`) - the whole window is engine code driven by config. Additive; all existing updater APIs unchanged.

- **Relaunch settle wait** (`KhaozEngine.Updates`). New `IUpdaterEnvironment.CanOpenExclusively(path)` (real: `File.Open(..., FileShare.None)` in a try/catch, disposed on success; returns true on non-Windows). `UpdateApplier.Apply` now, after the signature check + manifest install and before it relaunches, polls it until the game exe is openable (or after `SettleMaxPolls` x `SettlePollDelayMilliseconds` = 30s, relaunching anyway and logging the timeout). Rollback/abort paths relaunch the old, unscanned exe as before. Headless-tested: a fake env that reports the exe locked for N polls then openable proves the relaunch fires only once it is openable, and a never-openable env proves the timeout still relaunches.
- **Updater progress window** (`KhaozEngine.Updates`). New `IUpdaterUi` seam (`Show(theme)` / `SetPhase` / `SetProgress` / `SetStatus` / `Close`) with `UpdaterPhase { Download, Install, Finishing }`, a `UpdaterUiTheme` resolver, a no-op `NullUpdaterUi` (the default and every non-Windows platform), and a native `Win32UpdaterUi` (owner-drawn GDI bar in `WM_PAINT`, its own UI thread + message pump, updates marshalled via `PostMessage`, marquee during Finishing). `UpdateApplier.Apply` reports Install with per-file progress then Finishing during the settle wait and closes the window right before relaunch. `SystemUpdaterUi.CreateForCurrentOs` picks the Win32 window on Windows / the no-op elsewhere, wired in through `UpdateApplier.Run` by `UpdaterShim.Main`. The relocation dependency closure is unchanged (the UI is engine code already in the shim's closure and uses only OS P/Invoke).
- **Themeable UI config** (`KhaozEngine.Updates`). New optional `UpdateServiceOptions.UpdaterUi` (`UpdaterUiOptions`: window title, heading, accent/background/text `(R,G,B)` tuples, logo path, phase strings) serialized by `UpdateService.ApplyUpdate` into a new optional `ApplyUpdateConfig.Ui` block (`ApplyUpdateUiConfig` + `UpdaterUiColor`, registered on the source-generated `UpdatesJsonContext` so the trim/AOT shim reads it without reflection). Absent, everything still works. Round-trip + phase-order + theme-resolution tests added.

## 9.24.0

Runtime display settings: present mode / vsync, frame cap, window mode, and resolution are now all changeable live mid-session, not just at window construction. 9.23.0 shipped `PresentMode` + `FrameCapHz` but only applied present mode when the swapchain was first created; this closes the window/present side so a settings screen can flip everything at runtime with no crash and no leaked swapchain. New cohesive `IDisplaySettings` surface (present mode, frame cap, window mode, resolution) exposed on `AppWindow` and forwarded on the `GameApp` facade as `GameApp.Display`, plus per-setting pass-throughs. The Metal vsync reality is handled honestly: setting vsync reconfigures the live swapchain (reaching `CAMetalLayer.displaySyncEnabled`), but because the Veldrid Metal present still does not throttle the CPU from vsync alone, `FrameCapHz` remains the deterministic cap on macOS and the engine now warns once when vsync is selected with no frame cap on Metal. Additive; all existing APIs unchanged.

- **Runtime present-mode switch** (`KhaozEngine.Gpu` + `KhaozEngine.Windowing`). New settable `IGpuDevice.SyncToVerticalBlank` reconfigures the live Veldrid swapchain's vsync in place (no recreate, no leaked swapchain, size + depth preserved; a no-op mirrored value on a headless device where Veldrid would throw). `AppWindow.PresentMode` is now a get/set property (was construction-only) whose setter routes through it. On Metal this reaches `CAMetalLayer.displaySyncEnabled`.
- **Runtime window-mode + resolution** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`). New `WindowMode { Windowed, BorderlessFullscreen, ExclusiveFullscreen }` and settable `AppWindow.WindowMode`, plus `AppWindow.Resize(int, int)` for the windowed size in logical points. Window-state policy is the pure, headless-tested `WindowModePlanner.Compute` (maps a mode to Silk window state / border / geometry); the swapchain follows the new framebuffer via the existing `FramebufferResize` hook, so the HiDPI framebuffer semantics are unchanged (the backbuffer always tracks the physical drawable).
- **`IDisplaySettings` cohesive surface** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing` + `KhaozEngine.Game`). New `IDisplaySettings` (present mode, frame cap, window mode, resolution) and the `DisplaySettings` snapshot record (a `with`-friendly value type). `AppWindow` implements it (`CurrentDisplay` read + `ApplyDisplay` apply-all, safe mid-session); `GameApp` exposes it as `GameApp.Display` plus `PresentMode` / `FrameCapHz` / `WindowMode` / `Backend` pass-throughs. `GameAppOptions` gains an initial `WindowMode` (default `Windowed`).
- **Metal vsync warning** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`). Pure predicate `DisplaySettings.RequiresFrameCapWarning(backend, presentMode, frameCapHz)` (Metal + vsync + no cap). `AppWindow` emits a one-time `Console.Error` warning through it (via the `FrameCapHz` / `PresentMode` setters and `ApplyDisplay`), so a consumer selecting vsync on macOS is told to set `FrameCapHz` for a real cap. `PresentMode` docs updated to state `FrameCapHz` is the required deterministic cap on Metal.
- **Windowed smoke** (`KhaozEngine.Showcase`). The showcase gains app-level display hotkeys (F7 vsync, F8 frame cap, F9 window mode, F10 resolution) driven through `GameApp.Display`, with an on-screen readout of the live `DisplaySettings` + framebuffer size + backend - the manual verification that everything flips live with no crash.

## 9.23.0

Networked-movement presentation fix: remotes no longer hold-and-catch-up and the local camera no longer 30 Hz-sawtooths, on loopback at any render:tick ratio. Two independent presentation-layer defects, both traced to the tick beating against the render loop (not the network, not animation): (1) remote interpolation ran an estimate-the-inter-snapshot-interval-and-ramp-alpha scheme with no fixed delay buffer, so at a non-integer render:tick ratio the phase drifted each tick - alpha pinned at 1 and the remote **held** when a snapshot was a frame late, or **snapped** forward when early (~6-11% of frames were holds); (2) `ClientPrediction.Reconcile` collapsed the in-flight inter-tick interpolation onto the fresh authoritative basis every tick, leaving only the smoothing-offset decay to carry motion for the rest of the tick - a per-tick velocity dip that read as a 30 Hz sawtooth on a follow camera. Remote interpolation is now a **fixed-delay timestamped snapshot buffer** (render at `latest - InterpolationDelayTicks`, lerp the two bracketing snapshots by their true timestamps) and reconcile is **C1-continuous** (keeps the inter-tick phase flowing, folds only genuine misprediction into the decaying offset; a hard snap still collapses). Both are verified headless: a per-frame rendered-position trace at an integer (60/120) and a non-integer (~178 fps) render:tick ratio shows the remote with no hold frames and no catch-up snaps and the local player with no short-frame sawtooth. Also adds a present-mode / frame-cap dial (pin the render rate to an integer multiple of the tick) and a first-class presentation-trace diagnostic. Additive; the legacy `ClientReplicationView.Interpolate(alpha)` and all existing APIs are unchanged.

- **`WorldClient` remote interpolation is a fixed-delay snapshot buffer** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld` + `KhaozEngine.Replication`). New `ClientReplicationView.RecordInterpolationSample(t)` stamps each applied snapshot's interpolatable bytes into a per-component timestamped history, and `InterpolateAt(world, renderTime)` renders every component at `renderTime` by lerping the two buffered samples bracketing it by their true timestamps (clamp to the oldest before the buffer; HOLD at the newest past it - a genuine starvation hold, flagged by `WasHeldAtLastInterpolation(netId)`; single-sample renders that sample). `WorldClient.AdvancePresentation` drives it off a monotonic render clock at `presentationClock - InterpolationDelaySeconds`, decoupling presentation from the tick cadence and the render fps. The old `snapshotInterval` EMA + alpha ramp is gone. Delay tunable via new **`WorldClientConfig.InterpolationDelayTicks`** (default 2 ticks). A delta that removes an interpolatable component now purges its sample history, so `InterpolateAt` cannot resurrect it.
- **`ClientPrediction.Reconcile` is C1-continuous** (`KhaozEngine.Netcode`). A non-hard-snap rebase no longer collapses the inter-tick interpolation (previous position + elapsed) onto the new basis; it keeps that phase flowing at the steady velocity and folds only the genuine misprediction into the decaying render offset, so a matching (loopback) rebase perturbs neither the rendered position nor its velocity. A hard snap still collapses (an intentional teleport). Existing continuity / hard-snap / dead-zone tests unchanged.
- **Present mode + frame cap** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing` + `KhaozEngine.Game` + `KhaozEngine.Gpu`). New `PresentMode { Vsync, Immediate }` and `FrameLimiter` (a pure monotonic-clock scheduler). `AppWindow` gains a ctor overload taking `PresentMode` + `frameCapHz` and a settable `FrameCapHz` property (paces `Run` independently of vsync); `AppWindow.Scaled` forwards them. `GpuDeviceContext.CreateForWindow` takes `syncToVerticalBlank` (default true, feeds device options + swapchain). `GameAppOptions` gains `PresentMode` + `FrameCapHz` (default vsync, uncapped). Lets a game pin its render rate to an integer multiple of a fixed tick (e.g. 60/120 for 30 Hz) - the deterministic cap where the Veldrid Metal present does not throttle from vsync alone.
- **`PresentationTrace` diagnostic** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`). Debug-gated via **`WorldClientConfig.PresentationTraceEnabled`** (default off, zero overhead); `WorldClient.PresentationTrace` records per render frame, per rendered entity, the internal presentation signals a consumer cannot otherwise see - render clock, interpolation delay, render time, seconds-since-snapshot, snapshot-arrival marks, local reconcile-error, and the per-remote starvation-hold flag - plus rendered positions, dumpable to CSV (`WriteCsv`). The engine-side promotion of a throwaway client-side position logger.

## 9.22.1

Fix: a `ScrollablePanel` header drag that **grows** the panel no longer also scrolls the list. The panel makes header-resize and content-drag-pan mutually exclusive, but only latched it via the drag's press-origin: growing the panel docks its top upward, so `ContentBounds` rises past the fixed press-origin and `GetDragDelta`'s press-origin test starts matching, panning the list mid-resize (a consumer resizing a docked slide-up panel saw the content scroll while dragging the header up). The drag-pan is now gated on `!_resizing` as well, so a resize never scrolls regardless of how far the panel grows. Behaviour-only patch, no public API change; the wheel and content-drag paths are unchanged, and the existing drag-down resize test is joined by a drag-up regression test.

- **`ScrollablePanel`** (`KhaozEngine.Gui`) - `Update` skips the content drag-pan while `_resizing` is set (a header-resize in progress), instead of relying solely on `GetDragDelta`'s press-origin gate. Fixes the resize-grows-and-scrolls regression from the 9.21.0 overlay-chrome work.

## 9.22.0

Windows **taskbar-button icon** fix, take two: the running app's taskbar button now actually shows the app icon instead of the generic default. The 9.19.0 attempt (born-hidden + `WM_SETICON`-before-show + AppUserModelID) targeted the wrong icon slot and did nothing for the taskbar - testers confirmed it. Root cause: on Windows a top-level window has two independent icon slots. `WM_SETICON` (ICON_BIG/ICON_SMALL), which is all `glfwSetWindowIcon` (behind `AppWindow.SetIcon`) ever sets, drives the **title bar and Alt-Tab**; the **taskbar button** is resolved from the window **class** icon (`GCLP_HICON`/`GCLP_HICONSM`). GLFW registers its window class with the generic `IDI_APPLICATION` whenever the exe has no resource literally named `GLFW_ICON` - and a .NET `<ApplicationIcon>` is embedded under a different name, so GLFW never picks it up. Hence the exact split every consumer saw: correct title-bar icon, generic taskbar icon. The fix copies the icon the window already carries onto its class icon, so the taskbar button matches. Because `GameApp` sets the icon while the window is still hidden (the 9.19.0 born-hidden ordering, which is now genuinely load-bearing) and reveals it with `Show()` afterwards, the taskbar button is *born* with the right icon. No public API change, no consumer code change - a consumer already on the runtime-icon path (`WindowIcons`/`WindowIconPath`) gets the taskbar fix just by bumping the pin. AppUserModelID (9.19.0) stays for grouping/pinning. No-op off Windows, on a window with no icon, or with no native HWND; never throws.

- **`WindowsWindowIcon.TrySyncTaskbarIconFromWindow(nint hwnd)`** (`KhaozEngine.Platform`) - new guarded user32 P/Invoke that reads the window's live `WM_SETICON` handles (`WM_GETICON`) and assigns them to the window **class** icon (`SetClassLongPtrW` with `GCLP_HICON`/`GCLP_HICONSM`), so the Windows taskbar button shows the app icon. Reuses the HICONs GLFW built (no rebuild from pixels). Returns `false` off Windows, on a zero handle, or when the window has no icon to copy; never throws. Sibling to `WindowsAppId` and `ApplicationIcon`.
- **`AppWindow.SetIcon`** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`) now, on Windows, calls `WindowsWindowIcon.TrySyncTaskbarIconFromWindow` right after `SetWindowIcon` (passing the native Win32 HWND). Same signature and cross-platform behaviour; the only change is the added Windows class-icon sync. macOS (Dock icon via `SetMacDockIcon`) and Linux/X11 are unaffected no-ops.

## 9.21.0

Gui overlay chrome: `ScrollablePanel`, `Dropdown`, and `Tooltip` gain opt-in panel/overlay behaviours (sliding docked panels, a resizable header band, a scrim, a dropdown chevron, two-column tooltips, and touch auto-dismiss) so a game can retire its hand-rolled copies. Every knob defaults to a no-op, so existing callers render byte-identically and no public API breaks. Promoted from Nullwake's bespoke widgets and generalised (no game-specific coupling); all headless-tested. Additive minor.

- **`ScrollablePanel`** (`KhaozEngine.Gui`) - the caller-owned `Bounds` stays the docked, fully-open rect; new geometry is computed off `CurrentBounds`/`ContentBounds`, which equal `Bounds` when no knob is set (so the existing scroll/clip/hit-test path is unchanged). New opt-in members: `HeaderHeight` + `HeaderBackground`/`HeaderDivider`/`HeaderTextColor` + `DrawHeader(batch, white, font, title)` reserve a header band above the scroll region (content clips below it, `MaxScroll`/`ItemBounds`/`TappedItemIndex` all account for it); `TransitionAlpha` + `SlideFromBottom` map a 0..1 progress to a vertical slide up from the docked bottom edge; `Resizable` + `MinHeight`/`MaxHeight` let a drag on the header resize the panel (docked to the bottom, latched to the press-origin so it tracks past the moving header, and never scrolls the list); `Scrim` + `ScrimColor`/`ScrimAlpha` + `DrawScrim` draw a dimmed backdrop that reserves its own footprint and reports `ScrimDismissed` on a tap outside the panel. `HeaderBounds`/`ContentBounds`/`CurrentBounds` are exposed for layout.
- **`Dropdown`** (`KhaozEngine.Gui`) - `ShowChevron` (default false) draws a chevron caret on the right of the trigger that points down when closed and up when open (colour `ChevronColor`); `Opacity` (default 1) multiplies every colour's alpha at draw time so the whole dropdown can fade with a host transition. The two-phase `Draw`/`DrawOverlay` split, open/close, tap-outside dismiss, and hover/selected highlighting are unchanged.
- **`Tooltip`** (`KhaozEngine.Gui`) - a two-column title via `Show(title, titleRight, lines, anchor)` (right value measured with the body font, `TitleRightColor`, gap `TooltipMetrics.TitleRightGap`) and a matching `ComputeBounds` overload that widens the bubble to fit; `ShowTitleSeparator` + `SeparatorColor` draw a 1px rule under the title; and platform-aware dismissal via `Dismiss` (`TooltipDismiss.CallerDriven` default = desktop hover, unchanged; `TooltipDismiss.TapOutside` = touch, auto-hides on the next tap-outside when you call the new `Update(Pointer)`). The dismissal mode is a runtime value, not a compile-time platform branch. The pure `ShouldDismiss(...)` decision and the two-column `ComputeBounds` are headless-tested.
- **`GuiDraw`** (`KhaozEngine.Gui`, internal) - added shared primitives behind the above: `WithOpacity(color, opacity)` (alpha fade), `CaretGeometry`/`Caret` (the chevron), and `Line` (a rotated-quad line via the 1x1 white texture, since Render2D has no line primitive).
## 9.20.0

Speed-synced locomotion playback: an animated character's Walk/Run clip now advances in proportion to how fast it actually moves, so its feet stop sliding ("gliding") when the world speed differs from the speed the clip was authored to move at. A locomotion clip previously played at its authored rate no matter the character's real speed, so any character whose movement speed did not match the clip's authored ground speed slid its feet (Ruinborne's wolf glided, worked around by forcing the gallop clip; the player avatar had the same latent slide). Opt in per model by telling the brain the m/s each ground MOVE clip was authored to move at; it then advances that clip at `clamp(horizontalSpeed / referenceSpeed, min, max)`. Idle and the air states (Jump/Fall) always play at 1x. Additive minor, new public API only. **Default OFF** - every existing consumer is byte-identical until it opts in (new fields default to the current behaviour; `AnimationPlayer.Update(dt)` is exactly `Update(dt, 1f)`, an exact-`* 1` no-op).

- **`LocomotionSpeedSync`** (`KhaozEngine.Game.Render3D`) - new config struct describing speed-synced playback: `Enabled`, per-move-state reference speeds `WalkClipSpeed` / `RunClipSpeed` (m/s the clip was authored to move at), and clamp bounds `MinMultiplier` / `MaxMultiplier` (default `[0.25, 3.0]` via `DefaultMinMultiplier` / `DefaultMaxMultiplier`). `LocomotionSpeedSync.Enable(walkClipSpeed, runClipSpeed, minMultiplier?, maxMultiplier?)` builds an enabled config; `Disabled` (== `default`) is off. `RateFor(state, horizontalSpeed)` returns the playback multiplier: 1 when disabled, for Idle/Jump/Fall, or when the state's reference speed is `<= 0` (avoids divide-by-zero); otherwise `clamp(horizontalSpeed / referenceSpeed, min, max)`. Zero clamp bounds fall back to the defaults, so a field-initialised config never clamps to zero.
- **`AnimatedCharacter`** (`KhaozEngine.Game.Render3D`) - new final ctor parameter `LocomotionSpeedSync speedSync = default` (OFF by default, so the existing 5-arg ctor calls are unchanged). When enabled, a committed Walk/Run state advances its clip by `dt * speedSync.RateFor(State, horizontalSpeed)`; Idle and air states stay at 1x. Crossfade duration is unaffected.
- **`AnimationPlayer.Update(float dt, float speedMultiplier)`** (`KhaozEngine.Render3D`) - new overload that scales the clip playheads (both the incoming and the outgoing clip during a blend, so the feet track speed even mid-blend) by `speedMultiplier`, while the crossfade TIMER still runs at wall-clock `dt` so a blend completes in its authored duration regardless of speed. The existing `Update(dt)` is now `Update(dt, 1f)` - byte-identical (`* 1f` is exact).
- **`CharacterAnimatorTuning`** (`KhaozEngine.Game.Render3D`) - new fields `SyncLocomotionToSpeed` (opt-in flag, default false), `WalkClipSpeed` / `RunClipSpeed` (authored ground speeds), and `MinLocomotionRate` / `MaxLocomotionRate` (clamp bounds, default 0.25 / 3.0), plus a `SpeedSync()` helper that builds the `LocomotionSpeedSync` these fields describe. The convenience `ReplicatedCharacterAnimators(skeleton, clips, tuning)` ctor threads it into every brain it builds, so a consumer sets the reference speeds once per model. A `Func<AnimatedCharacter>` factory still owns its own sync config.

## 9.19.1

Fix: `WorldServer` and `ShardedWorldServer` now size their input command queue to `MaxPlayers`, so a server configured with more than 64 players no longer silently drops every move from the 65th-and-higher slot (a frozen avatar, no error). Both servers built their `RemoteCommandQueue<MoveCommand>` without a `maxSlots`, so it fell back to the queue's default distinct-slot cap of 64. `SlotAllocator` hands out slots in `[0, MaxPlayers)`, so on any server with `MaxPlayers > 64` the highest slots ran past that cap and `RemoteCommandQueue.Store` rejected their commands, freezing those avatars with no diagnostic. The queue is now constructed with `maxSlots: Math.Max(64, MaxPlayers)` in both servers, floored at 64 so a smaller `MaxPlayers` never shrinks it below the library default (a pure widening, no behaviour change for any game already at or below 64 players). Patch fix, no public API or config change.

- **`WorldServer` / `ShardedWorldServer`** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) - the per-slot input `RemoteCommandQueue<MoveCommand>` is now sized to `Math.Max(64, MaxPlayers)` distinct slots instead of the queue's default 64, so input for slots 64+ is processed rather than dropped. Regression covered by a headless test that joins 70 clients over the in-memory hub to each server and asserts every slot's move drives its avatar (pre-fix, slot 64 stayed frozen at spawn).

## 9.19.0

Windows running-app **taskbar icon** fix: a running desktop game's taskbar button now shows the app icon instead of the generic `.exe` placeholder. Two Windows-guarded, never-throwing, no-op-elsewhere changes cover the two causes. First, a per-game **AppUserModelID**: `GameAppOptions.AppUserModelId` (default null) sets the process's explicit Windows AppUserModelID before the first window is created, so Windows 10/11 keys the taskbar button to the app and resolves its icon (it also stabilises taskbar grouping and pinning). With no AUMID a .NET apphost gets a process-derived identity that fails to resolve the window/exe icon, which is why the running button showed the placeholder. Second, **icon-before-first-show ordering**: `AppWindow` is now born hidden and revealed by a new `Show()` after the runtime icon is applied, so the taskbar button (created when the window is first shown, keyed to whatever icon it has at that instant) is born with the correct `ICON_BIG` rather than GLFW's generic default that `WM_SETICON` later refreshes on the title bar but not on an already-created taskbar button. Additive minor, new public API only, backward compatible. Leaving `AppUserModelId` null keeps the current behaviour, the title-bar and Explorer `<ApplicationIcon>` icons are unchanged, and macOS (GLFW ignores window icons, Dock icon via `SetMacDockIcon`) plus Linux/X11 are unaffected no-ops.

- **`GameAppOptions.AppUserModelId`** (`KhaozEngine.Game`) - optional `string?`, default null. When set (e.g. `"APKiwi.Nullwake"`, a dotted `CompanyName.ProductName` by convention), `GameApp` calls `AppWindow.TrySetProcessAppUserModelId` as the FIRST step of its constructor, before the window is created. Null keeps the current process-derived identity. No-op off Windows.
- **`WindowsAppId.TrySetProcessAppUserModelId(string?)`** (`KhaozEngine.Platform`) - new guarded shell32 P/Invoke over `SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID` that sets the process's explicit AppUserModelID. Returns `false` off Windows, on a null/empty id, or on a failed shell call, and never throws. Sibling to `ApplicationIcon` (the macOS Dock-icon interop) in the same package.
- **`AppWindow.TrySetProcessAppUserModelId(string?)`** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`) - static forwarder to `WindowsAppId` so a bare `AppWindow` host can set the identity before constructing the window (it must run before the native window exists). Same no-op and never-throw contract.
- **`AppWindow.Show()`** (`KhaozEngine.Windowing`) - the window is now created hidden (`WindowOptions.IsVisible = false`) and `Show()` reveals it (idempotent). `GameApp` calls `SetIcon` then `Show` in its constructor so the taskbar button is born with the icon. `AppWindow.Run` also calls `Show()`, so a host that never calls it still gets a visible window. Only the pre-show timing changed, so a windowed app's on-screen behaviour is otherwise identical.

## 9.18.0

Per-client, area-of-interest-scoped **delta replication** on the live serving path: clients now receive only what changed inside their interest set each tick instead of a full snapshot of every in-AoI entity every tick, cutting the MMO stack's #1 bandwidth ceiling. Measured on a 16-player dense hotspot at 30 Hz with everyone idle: a full snapshot cost **~573 bytes/client/tick (~17.2 KB/s per client)**; the AoI delta costs **~25 bytes/client/tick (~0.75 KB/s per client)** - a **95%+** reduction, and static entities (NPCs, names) stop paying full freight every tick. Additive minor, new public API only; the full snapshot survives as the `baseline -1` delta so the wire is a strict superset, and client and server upgrade independently (an older client keeps getting full snapshots; an older server keeps being served them) with no disconnect - the same bar as 9.16.0. Reliability is phase 1: reliable-ordered, deltas built from each client's last acknowledged baseline, so a dropped delta/ack self-heals on the next tick.

- **`AoiDeltaReplicator`** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`) - the new per-client, `NetId`-keyed, AoI-aware baseline+delta encoder that fuses `ServerReplicator`'s acked-baseline delta compression with per-client interest filtering. `BeginTick()` opens a tick; `WriteFor(slot, world, interestSet)` emits, against that client's acknowledged baseline, an entity that **entered** the interest set as a full spawn, one that **stayed and changed** as only its changed components, one that **left** (or despawned) as a removal, and an unchanged in-AoI entity as nothing. `Acknowledge(slot, seq)` advances the baseline; `Forget(slot)` drops a disconnected client. The wire is byte-identical to `ServerReplicator.WriteFor`, so `ClientReplicationView.ApplyDelta` decodes both. Per-client memory is bounded by `historyDepth × players`. The baseline is keyed by `NetId`, not by owning cell, so a seamless cell handoff (an entity that stays in AoI while changing owning cell) reads as a component delta, never a despawn+respawn.
- **`ClientReplicationView.ApplyDelta` self-heal** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`) - now accepts a delta whose baseline is at or before `LastAppliedSeq` (an idempotent rebuild from the client's acked baseline, which lags what it has applied whenever an ack is in flight or was lost); only a baseline AHEAD of `LastAppliedSeq` throws. A `baseline -1` delta is now a full snapshot: entities the client still tracks but the delta omits are despawned (the same full-state semantics as `Apply`). The 9.16.0 skip-unknown-extension + malformed-length guards are unchanged.
- **Delta serving on both servers** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) - `WorldServer` and `ShardedWorldServer` serve delta-capable clients per-tick AoI deltas (the sharded one per home cell, so `NetId`-keying keeps a boundary crossing transparent) and full snapshots to everyone else. **`WorldServerConfig.DeltaReplication`** / **`ShardedWorldServerConfig.DeltaReplication`** gate it (default **true**; set false to force full snapshots). A slot is upgraded to deltas on the client's `DeltaCapable` hello and its baseline advances on each replication ack.
- **`ShardHost.HomeInterest(slot, interestRadius) -> (World, HashSet<int>)`** (`KhaozEngine.Sharding`) - exposes a client's home-cell world and AoI net-id set (the shared basis `SnapshotForClient` already used) so the server can drive the delta encoder over it. `SnapshotForClient` now delegates to it.
- **Client delta path + ack** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) - **`WorldClientConfig.RequestDeltaReplication`** (default **true**) makes `WorldClient` advertise `DeltaCapable` on join and apply `ServerFrameKind.Delta` frames (reconciling exactly as for a snapshot), acking each applied seq so the server advances its baseline. Against a server that predates the feature it transparently keeps receiving full snapshots and sends no acks.
- **Wire additions** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld` `MoveProtocol`) - **`ServerFrameKind.Delta`** (same `[localNetId][ackSeq]` header as a snapshot, gated to delta-capable clients so an older client only ever gets `Snapshot`); **`ClientControlKind.DeltaCapable`** (a 2-byte join hello an older server decodes as an unknown control and harmlessly ignores); and **`EncodeReplicationAck` / `TryDecodeReplicationAck`** (a 6-byte ack, distinct in length from a move or a control).
- **`MmoServerSample`** - the reference `MmoServer` now serves per-client AoI deltas (with a small client ack), demonstrating the delta path end to end including skip-unknown-extension on the delta wire.

## 9.17.0

World-space **nameplate** widget in `KhaozEngine.Render3D`: an MMO-style plate (a rounded panel holding a centred name and one or more health/resource bars) that supersedes the text-only `WorldLabel`, driven by a data-model so a game ships one bar now and adds more (or badges/subtitle/level) later without a rewrite. Additive minor, new public API only, no breaking changes: `WorldLabel` is untouched. Lives beside `WorldLabel`, projects the head via `IIsoCamera3D.WorldToScreen`, draws screen-space (not depth-tested) after the 3D pass, and reuses `SpriteBatch.DrawRounded` on the white texture (the `DiagnosticsOverlay` convention). Bundled in the `Game3D` umbrella, so a `Game3D` consumer (Ruinborne) reaches it with no new reference.

- **`Nameplate`** (`KhaozEngine.Render3D`) - the data model: `Title` + `TitleColor` + `Bars` (an `IReadOnlyList<NameplateBar>`, may be empty for a title-only plate). `Nameplate.IsEmpty` (blank title AND no bars) is the render-free cull predicate. `badges` / `subtitle` / `level` are called out as future additive fields, deliberately not added yet.
- **`NameplateBar`** (readonly struct) - one bar: `Fraction`, `Fill`, `Track`, and a reserved `Overlay` string (e.g. "100/100", NOT drawn in v1). `NameplateBar.ClampedFraction` exposes the 0..1-clamped fill the renderer draws with.
- **`NameplateStyle`** (readonly struct) - the look, split from the data: panel fill/border/thickness, corner radius, `PadX`/`PadY`, `BarHeight`/`BarSpacing`/`BarCornerRadius`, `MinBarWidth`, `FontScale`, `MaxWidth` (0 = unbounded, else the title is ellipsized to fit), and an optional `TitleShadow`/`TitleShadowOffset`. **`NameplateStyle.Default`** is the unified opaque-plate preset; drop `PanelFill` alpha to 0 and set `TitleShadow` (via a `with` expression) for the panel-less "classic pill" look, so one widget covers all three archetypes.
- **`NameplateLayout.Measure(ITextMeasurer font, in Nameplate, in NameplateStyle) -> Vector2`** - pure, GPU-free panel-size math (title width floored to `MinBarWidth` + padding; title row + stacked bars + spacing; capped at `MaxWidth`). Headless-testable with a fake measurer.
- **`NameplateRenderer.Draw(batch, font, white, camera, worldPos, offset, in plate, in style, viewportW, viewportH, maxDistance = 0, cullFrom = null) -> bool`** - projects `worldPos + offset`, centres the panel on the head pixel and bottom-anchors it, then draws the panel (fill + optional border), the centred title (shadow pass first if set), and each bar (track then `Fraction`-wide fill). Returns `false` on cull (empty plate, behind camera, off-screen, beyond `maxDistance`). No per-frame heap allocation. **`NameplateRenderer.ShouldCull(worldPos, cullFrom, maxDistance)`** shares `WorldLabel.ShouldCull`, so plates and labels cull identically.

## 9.16.0

Server-owned non-player entity (NPC / enemy) replication seam: a game can now replicate its own components on top of the movement protocol and read them per-entity on the client, so a server-spawned NPC is drawable as something other than a player. Adds a consumer-injectable `ReplicationRegistry` on both servers plus the client, `WorldClient.TryGetComponent<T>`, `ShardedWorldServer.SpawnEntity` / `OnBeforeTick` (with `WorldServer` parity), and a forward-compatible wire change where consumer "extension" component ids are length-prefixed so an older client skips one it never registered instead of disconnecting. Additive minor, new public API, every new param / hook defaults to today's behaviour. The built-in movement wire (ids 1 / 2 / 3) is byte-identical, so existing snapshots are unchanged.

- **Consumer extension components + skip-unknown wire** (`KhaozEngine.Replication`):
  - **`ReplicationRegistry.FirstExtensionTypeId`** (= 16) and **`ReplicationRegistry.IsExtension(ushort)`** - the documented floor. Component type ids at/above it are CONSUMER extension ids. Ids `1..15` stay reserved for engine built-ins.
  - Extension components are **length-prefixed on the wire** (`[typeId][7-bit len][data]`), so a client whose registry never registered that id **skips** it (ignores the component) instead of failing the snapshot. `SnapshotWriter` (full-state + `WriteFiltered`) and `ServerReplicator` (baseline / delta) both frame them. `ClientReplicationView.Apply` / `ApplyDelta` skip an unknown extension id and hostile-safely reject a corrupt length. An unknown BUILT-IN id (below the floor) is unchanged: still a hard "client out of date" mismatch (surfaced as `DisconnectReason.IncompatibleVersion`). Built-in ids `1..15` keep their exact unframed encoding, so existing wire bytes are identical.
- **Consumer-injectable registry** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`):
  - **`MoveProtocol.CreateRegistry(Action<ReplicationRegistry>? configure)`** - build the movement registry and register your own components (at ids >= **`MoveProtocol.FirstConsumerTypeId`**) in one call, used identically on server and client.
  - **`WorldServer`** / **`ShardedWorldServer`** / **`WorldClient`** each take an optional `ReplicationRegistry? registry` ctor param (default = movement-only). The server and client must be built with the same extended registry.
- **`WorldClient.TryGetComponent<T>(int netId, out T)`** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) - reads a replicated component off the entity with that net id (the `EntityRenderState.Id` value). The client-side seam for reading a server-assigned discriminator (NPC kind, HP, faction) to pick a model. Returns `false` against an older server that never sends `T` (no handshake, no disconnect).
- **`ShardedWorldServer.SpawnEntity(float x, float z, Action<World, Entity>? configure)`** (`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`) - spawns a server-owned non-player entity, allocating a non-colliding `NetId` from the authoritative allocator (honours the `CellPersistence` high-water) and placing it in the owning cell. `configure` adds game components. Persisted with its cell, replicated through the normal AoI + ghost + handoff pipeline. **`WorldServer.SpawnEntity`** is the single-world equivalent.
- **`ShardedWorldServer.OnBeforeTick` / `WorldServer.OnBeforeTick`** (`event Action<float>?`) - fired at the start of `Tick(dt)` before the snapshot pass, where an NPC / enemy brain runs each tick and writes `ReplicatedPosition` so its move reaches clients the same tick. No-op until subscribed.
- **`MmoServerSample`** demonstrates the seam end to end: a `Creature` extension component (a kind discriminator) registered above the floor, `SpawnNpc(x, y, kind)` built on a public `SpawnEntity(x, y, configure)`, players carry none (so a client tells NPCs apart), and an older client without `Creature` still applies the snapshot.

## 9.15.0

Anti-aliasing options: a unified `AntiAliasing` selection (None / FXAA / MSAA / SSAA) on `PixelPostProcessSettings.Quality`, plus the machinery behind each mode - the SSAA downscale is now a correct mip-filtered box at ANY factor (not just 2), a new FXAA post pass, and real hardware MSAA threaded through the GPU abstraction. Every game gets the AA dropdown most ship, validated against the device (never throws). Additive minor, new public API, default `None` so existing scenes are byte-identical (verified across the GPU golden net) until a game opts in.

- **`AntiAliasing` / `AntiAliasingMode` / `RenderQuality`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Render3D`) - the settings surface:
  - **`AntiAliasingMode`** = `None` / `Fxaa` / `Msaa` / `Ssaa`.
  - **`AntiAliasing`** (immutable value) built with `AntiAliasing.Off` / `.Fxaa` / `.Msaa(samples)` / `.Ssaa(factor)`.
    **`ResolveFor(in GpuCapabilities)`** clamps a request to the device (MSAA down to the largest supported
    power-of-two `<= MaxMsaaSampleCount`, or to FXAA if the device can't MSAA at all; SSAA/FXAA/None pass through) so
    an unsupported menu choice degrades gracefully instead of throwing.
  - **`RenderQuality`** - the extension point (holds `AntiAliasing` today; room for future anisotropy / shadow /
    texture / TAA knobs), reachable as **`PixelPostProcessSettings.Quality`**. Default `AntiAliasing.Off`, so the
    low-level `RenderScale` / `Supersample` / `Pixelated` fields still govern (back-compat). A non-None mode overrides
    the matching field (SSAA forces `MatchViewport` + drives `Supersample`); the `Pixelated` retro path forces AA off.
- **SSAA correct at any factor** - `RenderScale.MatchViewport` supersampling now downsamples through a mip-filtered
  (trilinear) blit instead of a single bilinear tap: the internal target carries a mip chain regenerated per frame
  and the final blit samples LOD `~= log2(factor)`, so `Supersample = 3` / `4` (or `AntiAliasing.Ssaa(3f)`)
  anti-alias properly rather than under-sampling above 2:1. Gated strictly to the MatchViewport downscale, so
  `FixedInternal` and the `Pixelated` path stay single-mip and byte-identical. Fixes the "can only safely go to 2x"
  footgun from 9.13.0.
- **FXAA** - a cheap fullscreen post pass (Timothy Lottes FXAA3-console) added to the pixel-post chain, toggled by
  `AntiAliasing.Fxaa`. Softens high-contrast edges (geometry AND shaded interiors) in one pass; preserves the
  background alpha marker so the starfield / transparent-preview paths still work; bypassed by `Pixelated`.
- **MSAA** - hardware multisampling of the 3D geometry pass, selected by `AntiAliasing.Msaa(2|4|8)`. Threaded through
  the GPU abstraction: **`GpuTextureDescription.SampleCount`** + **`IGpuTexture.SampleCount`**,
  **`GpuOutputDescription.SampleCount`** / **`WithSampleCount`**, **`IGpuCommandList.ResolveTexture`** (the MSAA
  resolve), and **`GpuCapabilities.MaxMsaaSampleCount`** (read from the device's per-format sample-count limit). The
  model MRT renders multisampled and resolves to single-sample targets before the post chain. MSAA anti-aliases
  geometry EDGES only, not shaded texture interiors, so it does NOT fix high-frequency terrain/foliage shimmer (use
  SSAA/FXAA for that); it is the cheap tool for foliage / edge crawl.
- Costs: SSAA is ~factor^2 fragment shading (`3` = 9x), MSAA adds a per-frame resolve, FXAA one fullscreen pass.
  Keep AA off by default and measure on the target GPU. Changing the MSAA sample count rebuilds the 3D pipelines
  (a menu-apply cost, not per-frame); loaded meshes' materials survive it.
- Tests: headless coverage of the settings resolution + device clamping (`AntiAliasingTests`) and the mip-downsample
  decision (`RenderScaleTests`); GPU tests that SSAA reduces high-frequency energy monotonically at factor 1/2/3
  (`SupersampleDownsampleGpuTests`), FXAA adds anti-aliased edge pixels (`FxaaGpuTests`), the MSAA GPU plumbing
  resolves on-device (`MsaaGpuTests`), and MSAA anti-aliases geometry edges end-to-end through Scene3D
  (`MsaaSceneGpuTests`). The whole GPU golden net is unchanged (default path byte-identical).

## 9.14.0

String-catalog lookup: `IStringCatalog` + `ResourceStringCatalog` resolve UI strings by key against `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` over a standard-library `ResourceManager`, and `LocalizationManager.Catalog` hands one out over the same resources the manager was built with. The reusable other half of the localization domain (the engine already shipped culture discovery + switching), so every game gets it instead of writing its own. Additive minor, new public API in `KhaozEngine.App`, no behaviour change to existing packages and no new dependency (App still depends only on Diagnostics).

- **`IStringCatalog`** (new, `KhaozEngine.App`) - `Get(key)` resolves against `CurrentUICulture` and returns the
  key itself when absent (a visible, non-fatal placeholder; never throws); `Format(key, args)` is a culture-aware
  `string.Format(CurrentUICulture, Get(key), args)` of the resolved template; `TryGet(key, out value)` is a
  non-throwing probe (false with `value == key` when absent, true + the value when present). Kept separate from
  `LocalizationManager` so key lookup and culture switching stay single-responsibility and composable.
- **`ResourceStringCatalog(ResourceManager)`** (new, `sealed`) - the standard-library-backed implementation.
  `Get` is `GetString(key, CurrentUICulture) ?? key`; it reads the current UI culture live, so a
  `LocalizationManager.SetCulture` takes effect immediately without re-creating the catalog. Pure BCL, no bespoke
  catalog format. Null `ResourceManager` throws `ArgumentNullException` at construction.
- **`LocalizationManager.Catalog`** (new `IStringCatalog` property) - a `ResourceStringCatalog` over the same
  `ResourceManager` the manager was constructed with, so a consumer wires culture discovery/switching and key
  lookup from one object: `var loc = new LocalizationManager(rm); IStringCatalog strings = loc.Catalog;`. A
  convenience factory only - it does not merge the two types into one facade.
- Tests: present key resolves to its localized value, an absent key returns the key (no throw), `TryGet` returns
  false + the key when absent (true + value when present), `Format` substitutes args into the resolved template,
  and a second `SetCulture` flips `Get` to the new culture's value (proves it reads `CurrentUICulture` live).

## 9.13.0

Supersampling (SSAA) for the 3D pass: `PixelPostProcessSettings.Supersample` renders the internal target at a multiple of the framebuffer under `RenderScale.MatchViewport`, then downsamples in the final blit. Anti-aliases BOTH geometry edges and shaded texture interiors (unlike MSAA), which fixes high-frequency-terrain / thin-foliage shimmer that "vibrates" when the camera moves on a standard-DPI display. Additive minor, default off (1x).

- **`PixelPostProcessSettings.Supersample`** (new, `float`, default `1`). Only affects `RenderScale.MatchViewport`
  (ignored for `FixedInternal`). The 3D internal target is rendered at framebuffer x this factor per axis and the
  final blit downsamples it, so it super-samples the whole shaded image. `2` = 2x per axis (4x the pixels), the same
  effective AA a 2x/Retina display gives for free - on a standard-DPI display it removes the motion shimmer that a
  Retina display never showed. The supersized target is still clamped to `MaxRenderWidth`/`MaxRenderHeight` (aspect
  preserved), so a big window x a big factor cannot allocate an unbounded target. A factor of 2 resolves with a
  correct 2x2 box through the existing bilinear blit; above ~2x the single-tap blit under-samples (mip the target
  for higher factors - future).
- Why not MSAA: MSAA only covers geometry-edge coverage, not shaded texture interiors, so it would miss the
  dominant symptom here (a high-frequency terrain albedo aliasing at grazing angles). SSAA covers both.
- Tests: `RenderScaleTests` gains supersample cases (2x below/at/over the cap, sub-1x clamp, FixedInternal ignores it).

Wall-clock resume detection: `GameClock` now reports the real time elapsed between frames from a UTC wall clock (which survives an OS sleep/suspend/hibernate, where the frame `dt` does not), and `GameApp` raises a new `OnResume` hook when that gap is large, so a game can run offline/AFK catch-up, re-sync timers, or pause. Additive minor, new public API, no behaviour change to existing packages (the 0.1s sim-delta clamp and `Dt` are unchanged).

- **`GameClock.RealWallGapSeconds` / `GameClock.LastRealTimestamp`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Windowing`) - each `Update` samples `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` and reports the wall-clock seconds since the previous frame (clamped to `>= 0`, so an NTP/DST backward step reads 0), plus the timestamp of that sample. Normally ~one frame; it spikes after an OS suspend or a long hang. A separate signal from the QueryPerformanceCounter-backed frame `dt`, which does not reliably advance across S3/hibernate. 0 on the first frame.
- **`GameApp.OnResume(TimeSpan wallGap)`** (new virtual, `KhaozEngine.Game`) - raised once, before `OnUpdate`, on the first frame whose `RealWallGapSeconds` exceeds **`GameAppOptions.ResumeGapThresholdSeconds`** (new, default 30s via `For()`; 0 or negative disables). Never fires on the first frame. Override it for suspend/resume offline catch-up (e.g. a one-shot `TimeSkip.Advance`), timer re-sync, or an auto-pause. `GameApp3D` inherits it unchanged.
- Tests: headless coverage of the wall-clock gap (frame-1 zero, per-frame-not-cumulative, backward-step clamp, independence from the sim-delta clamp, measured while paused) and the resume fire decision (fires once above threshold with the right span, not on frame 1 / below threshold / a backward step / when disabled).

## 9.11.0

Diagnostics: the live device now surfaces its adapter name and sampler feature flags, and `AppWindow` exposes the physical framebuffer (render) resolution and logical window size. Additive minor, new public read-only info (used to chase the Windows/D3D11 terrain fuzz from an in-game debug panel).

- **`GpuCapabilities`** (`KhaozEngine.Gpu`) gains **`DeviceName`** (the GPU adapter / driver name, Veldrid
  `GraphicsDevice.DeviceName`), **`SamplerAnisotropy`**, and **`SamplerLodBias`** (the `GraphicsDeviceFeatures`
  flags the sampler path already gates on - when false, a requested anisotropy/mip-LOD-bias is silently dropped).
  Reachable via `GpuDeviceContext.Capabilities` / `AppWindow.Capabilities`. The new ctor params are optional, so
  existing construction is unchanged.
- **`AppWindow.FramebufferWidth` / `FramebufferHeight`** (physical drawable pixels - the real render resolution;
  2x logical on Retina) and **`AppWindow.LogicalWidth` / `LogicalHeight`** (logical points). Their ratio is the
  DPI scale; a framebuffer below the monitor's native pixels means the OS is upscaling the window.
- Tests: headless `GpuCapabilitiesDiagTests` (field storage + never-null device name) and a gated live-device check
  (Metal reports `Apple M2 Max`, `SamplerAnisotropy=true`, `SamplerLodBias=false`).

## 9.10.0

Engine-owned Discord: a provider-neutral social/presence seam (`KhaozEngine.Social`) plus a pure-managed Discord Rich Presence backend (`KhaozEngine.Social.Discord`), so games retire their bespoke Discord code. Additive minor, new packages, no behaviour change to existing packages.

- **`KhaozEngine.Social`** (new, `Foundation` umbrella, deps: `Diagnostics`) - the seam:
  - **`ISocialProvider`** - provider-neutral contract: `TryInitialize`, `IsConnected`, `Update`, `SetPresence(in RichPresence)`, `ClearPresence`, `TryGetLocalUser(out SocialUser)`, and the `JoinRequested` / `JoinRequestReceived` events. Every method is best-effort and never throws.
  - **Value types** - `RichPresence` (details/state/timestamps/images/party/secrets/buttons), `PresenceImage`, `PresenceParty`, `PresenceButton`, `SocialUser`, `JoinRequest`.
  - **`NullSocialProvider`** - silent no-op default (headless servers, CI, no backend added).
  - **`SocialPresenceController`** - game-facing orchestration over any provider: lazy init, dedupe, throttled republish (`SocialPresenceOptions.RepublishInterval`, default 15s), an elapsed-timer helper (`SetElapsedPresence`), and session self-disable so a platform failure never reaches the game loop.
- **`KhaozEngine.Social.Discord`** (new, opt-in, NOT in any umbrella; add explicitly like `Physics.Bepu`, deps: `KhaozEngine.Social`) - **`DiscordSocialProvider : ISocialProvider`** over a pure-managed Discord IPC client (Windows named pipe / macOS+Linux unix domain socket, opcode+length+JSON framing via System.Text.Json). No native libraries, no third-party NuGet. Rich presence, local Discord identity, and join (`ACTIVITY_JOIN` / `ACTIVITY_JOIN_REQUEST`). `DiscordSocialOptions` carries the game's Discord Application id.
- The native Discord Social SDK (friends/lobbies/voice) is deliberately out of scope; if ever needed it slots in behind the same `ISocialProvider` as a separate opt-in `.Native` backend.
- Tests: headless coverage of the Null provider, the controller (dedupe/throttle/elapsed/self-disable), the IPC frame codec, activity payload mapping + dispatch parsing, unix socket path discovery, and the IPC client + provider against an in-memory transport. A live-socket smoke test is tagged `[Trait("Category","LiveSocket")]` and excluded from CI.

## 9.9.0

Diagnostic mip-chain readback: a game/test can read one mip level of a splat material's albedo array back to the CPU, to verify a generated mip chain on a real device (used to chase the Windows/D3D11 terrain "fuzz"). Additive minor, new public API, no behaviour change.

- **`Scene3D.DebugReadSplatAlbedoMip(SplatMaterialHandle, int mipLevel, int arrayLayer, out int width, out int height)`**
  (new, `KhaozEngine.Render3D`) returns that mip level of the material's albedo texture array as packed RGBA8 (its
  own dimensions in the `out` params). A high mip that is a real blurred downsample keeps mip 0's average colour and
  has much less local detail; a mip that is near-black (empty) or still detailed (a copy of mip 0) reveals broken GPU
  mip generation on that device.
- **`GpuReadback.ToRgbaMip(IGpuDevice, IGpuTexture, uint mipLevel, uint arrayLayer, int mipWidth, int mipHeight)`**
  (new, `KhaozEngine.Gpu`) - the general reusable primitive (copies the subresource into a staging texture, maps,
  de-strides), and **`IGpuCommandList.CopyTextureSubresource(src, srcMip, srcLayer, dst, width, height)`** underneath
  it (copy one mip/array-layer subresource into another texture's mip 0). The pre-existing whole-texture
  `CopyTexture` / `ToRgba` are unchanged.
- Tests: gated `SplatAlbedoMipReadbackGpuTests` proves a high mip of a procedural splat material is a real blurred
  downsample on the local device (mean preserved, detail collapses).

## 9.8.0

The macOS Dock / Cmd-Tab icon can now be set at runtime, so an unbundled `dotnet run` app (which has no `.app` bundle icns) shows a real icon instead of the generic document page. Additive minor; nothing changes on Windows/Linux or for a game that sets no icon.

- **`ApplicationIcon.TrySetMacDockIcon(byte[] pngBytes)`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Platform`) - sets the running app's
  macOS Dock icon from PNG bytes via `NSApplication.setApplicationIconImage:` (self-contained libobjc interop,
  mirroring `ClipboardInterop`'s autorelease-pool + `objc_msgSend` pattern). Returns `false` off macOS, on
  null/empty input, or on any Cocoa failure; never throws. GLFW cannot set the Cocoa Dock icon (so
  `AppWindow.SetIcon` stays a documented no-op there) and an unbundled run has no `.app` icns, so this is the only
  way such a run gets a real Dock icon.
- **`AppWindow.SetMacDockIcon(byte[] pngBytes)`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Windowing`) - the windowing-layer entry point,
  delegating to `ApplicationIcon`. The Cocoa counterpart to `SetIcon`.
- **`GameApp`** now drives it automatically: when `GameAppOptions.WindowIconPath` is set, on macOS it feeds that PNG
  to `SetMacDockIcon` right after the window exists (so the shared `NSApplication` GLFW created is live). A
  `WindowIcons`-only config (already-decoded RGBA, no PNG path) leaves the Dock icon untouched, since `NSImage`
  decodes from the PNG.
- **`KhaozEngine.Showcase`** ships an `assets/icon.png` and sets `WindowIconPath`, so the menu-hub run now carries a
  Dock icon on macOS (and a title-bar/taskbar icon on Windows/Linux) instead of the blank document icon.

## 9.7.0

Terrain/splat materials can now override how the ground samples its detail textures at a distance (anisotropy level, filter, mip LOD bias), so a game can trade grazing sharpness for less distance "fuzz". Additive minor, opt-in; a material that sets no override is byte-identical to before.

- **`TerrainSamplerConfig`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Render3D`) - a `readonly struct` of `Filter`
  (`GpuSamplerFilter`: anisotropic / trilinear / point), `MaximumAnisotropy`, and `MipLodBias`.
  `TerrainSamplerConfig.Default` is anisotropic 16x + a +1 mip bias, exactly the shared sampler the splat renderer
  already builds, so `Default` (and a null override) reproduce prior behaviour. Addressing is always Wrap (the
  detail textures tile).
- **`TerrainLayeredMaterial.Sampler`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Terrain`, `TerrainSamplerConfig?`) and a new trailing
  **`sampler`** parameter on **`Scene3D.LoadSplatMaterial(...)`** (default `null`). When set, the material builds and
  owns its own sampler (disposed with the material) instead of binding the renderer's shared one; when null it binds
  the shared default, so existing callers and the committed splat goldens are unchanged (no re-bake).
- Why: a high-frequency tiling albedo can shimmer/"fuzz" as the camera moves because 16x anisotropy keeps the
  grazing floor sharp (worst at grazing incidence, e.g. flat ground; better on steeper slopes). Lowering the
  anisotropy, switching to trilinear, or raising the mip bias blurs the far ground and reduces the aliasing. The
  right value is content-dependent, so it is a per-material knob rather than a changed default.
- `ModelRenderer` gains a `CreateSplatMaterialSet(..., IGpuSampler sampler)` overload and
  `CreateTerrainSampler(in TerrainSamplerConfig)`; the shared default sampler path is unchanged. Tests: headless
  `TerrainSamplerConfigTests` (defaults + null default) and a gated `TerrainSamplerOverrideGpuTests` (a material with
  a trilinear/high-bias override renders textured on a real device).

## 9.6.2

`SpriteBatch` no longer tears its 2D draws for a frame when a widget moves or resizes: the per-flush vertex buffers are now ring-buffered across frames instead of one buffer reused every frame. Render-only bug fix, no public API change. Fixes the F2 collision legend in Ruinborne flickering out for a single frame as the adjacent DIAG panel resized.

- **`SpriteBatch`** (`KhaozEngine.Render2D`, internal) kept one growable vertex buffer per flush and rewrote it
  every frame with a device-level `UpdateBuffer`, while the frame loop (`AppWindow.Run`) submits + presents with no
  `WaitForIdle`. So the CPU runs ahead and a frame's write to a reused buffer can race the GPU still reading it for
  an earlier, still-in-flight present. The result is a 1-frame tear that only surfaces when the buffer *contents*
  change frame-to-frame: a moving/resizing widget writes different bytes mid-read, whereas static content writes
  identical bytes so the race is invisible (why it looked like an intermittent, "every few seconds" flicker of only
  the thing that was moving). The 3D overlay/decal renderers never had this because they record their buffer writes
  into the command list (`cl.UpdateBuffer`), which is ordered against the prior frame.
- The per-flush buffers are now **ring-buffered `RingDepth` (= 3) frames deep**: `NewFrame` rotates to the next of
  three slots (slot = `_frame % RingDepth`), so a slot is not rewritten until three frames later, by which point
  its prior GPU reads have retired. Triple-buffering covers the CPU running up to two frames ahead. This also makes
  the grow-time `Dispose` of a slot's old buffer safe (that buffer was last used three frames ago). No behaviour
  change to any drawing API; buffers still persist and only grow.
- **New GPU test `SpriteBatchBufferRingTests`** drives the batch frame-by-frame and asserts the flush-0 buffer
  rotates through distinct instances and repeats every `RingDepth` frames (it would fail on the old single-buffer
  code, which returned the same instance every frame).

## 9.6.1

The terrain splat shader now samples with explicit gradients (`textureGrad`), fixing undefined mip/anisotropic LOD selection under the per-layer weight branch, the likely cause of the distant ground "fuzz"/pixelation reported on Direct3D11 (Windows) while Metal looked fine. Render-only bug fix, no public API change.

- **`SplatFrag`** (`KhaozEngine.Render3D`, internal) computed each triplanar texture sample with the implicit-LOD
  `texture()` inside the `for (int L...) { if (wl <= 0.001) continue; ... }` per-layer loop. Implicit LOD needs
  screen-space derivatives that are only defined in quad-uniform control flow; taken under that data-dependent
  `continue` the mip/aniso LOD is undefined, so on a diverging quad a backend may collapse toward mip 0 and the
  minified, high-frequency tiling ground aliases frame-to-frame as the camera moves. D3D11/FXC and Metal resolve
  that undefined case differently, which matches the Windows-bad / mac-fine report.
- The fix hoists `dFdx(vWorldPos)` / `dFdy(vWorldPos)` to uniform flow once before the loop and passes the
  per-plane gradients (scaled by each layer's tile rate) to `textureGrad`, so the LOD is well-defined regardless
  of the branch and the existing anisotropy + `mipLodBias` still apply to a real gradient. The blend math, the
  aniso-16 + `mipLodBias:1` terrain sampler (`ModelRenderer`), and the Metal output are unchanged (the model/prop
  pass and its goldens are untouched; on Metal the analytic gradients already matched the implicit ones, so the
  splat goldens pass with no re-bake).
- **New GPU golden `SplatTerrainDistanceGoldenTests`** renders the splat pass through a perspective camera at a
  grazing distance over a high-frequency checkerboard, closing a coverage gap: the pre-existing splat golden frames
  the ground with the orthographic iso camera nearly top-down, so it has no perspective minification and could
  never exhibit distance shimmer. The class is `*Golden*`-named, so the `cross-platform-gpu` matrix runs it on
  Metal / D3D11-WARP / Vulkan and it logs the per-backend near/far high-frequency energy for the first time. Its
  hard assertions are backend-robust (distant ground must render textured + lit) rather than a calibrated aliasing
  threshold, which only real per-backend numbers can set.
- Source-texture frequency is still the underlying driver of the shimmer (a 1024px albedo tiled every few metres
  minifies hard at distance); the sampler + `textureGrad` levers reduce the aliasing, they do not remove a
  too-noisy source. A consumer with a high tile rate should also lower it.

## 9.6.0

`OverlayLegend` gains a `Theme` + an explicit-position `Draw` overload + a `Bounds` rect, and `DiagnosticsOverlay` gains a `Bounds` rect, so two debug panels can sit side by side in a shared style instead of overlapping in the same corner. Additive minor, no breaking change.

- **`OverlayLegendTheme`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Gui`) - injected look + layout for `OverlayLegend` (panel fill,
  border, label colour, border thickness, padding, swatch size/gap, row spacing, text scale, and a
  `Corner`/`Margin` anchor). `Default` reproduces the neutral grey palette the legend shipped with, so existing
  callers are byte-identical. `FromDiagnostics(DiagnosticsOverlayTheme)` derives a matching palette (fill, border,
  near-white label from the diagnostics *value* text, thickness, padding, corner/margin, text scale) so a legend
  drawn next to a `DiagnosticsOverlay` shares its look; legend-specific layout (swatch size/gap, row spacing)
  keeps its own defaults. `Anchor(Rect viewport, float w, float h)` is the font-free corner-placement helper
  (headless-tested).
- **`OverlayLegend.Theme`** (new) + ctor param, and the widget now draws from the theme instead of hard-coded
  constants/colours (default look unchanged). **`OverlayLegend.Draw(SpriteBatch, SpriteFont, Texture2D, Vector2 topLeft)`**
  (new overload) places the panel at an explicit top-left instead of the theme corner - use it to sit the legend
  beside another panel. The existing `Draw(..., Rect viewport)` now anchors to `Theme.Corner`/`Theme.Margin`
  (default top-left + 12, matching prior behaviour). **`OverlayLegend.Bounds`** (new) exposes the last-drawn panel
  rect (empty when the last draw was a no-op).
- **`DiagnosticsOverlay.Bounds`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Gui`) - the last-drawn panel rect (empty when hidden / faded
  out / empty). A caller draws the diagnostics overlay top-left, then places an `OverlayLegend` at
  `Bounds.Right + gap` to put a second panel directly beside it.

## 9.5.1

`ScreenStack` now orders screens with a stable insert, so screens sharing a `DrawOrder` keep insertion order and `Screens[^1]` is reliably the visually-topmost. Bug fix, no API change. Before this, `Add` re-sorted the list with the non-stable `List.Sort`, which for larger stacks could reorder equal-`DrawOrder` screens and break code relying on last-is-topmost (for example an Esc-pops-topmost handler over a hosted screen stack). Small stacks were unaffected because `List.Sort` falls back to a stable insertion sort below its introsort threshold.

## 9.5.0

Terrain sampler gains anisotropy + a mip LOD bias to tame the distance/grazing "fuzz" a high-frequency tiling albedo (e.g. a noisy grass texture) shimmers into as the camera moves. Additive minor, one new public sampler field.

- **`GpuSamplerDescription.MipLodBias`** (new, `KhaozEngine.Gpu`) - a whole-mip-level bias added to the computed
  LOD (maps to Veldrid `SamplerDescription.LodBias`). A positive value biases sampling toward blurrier mips, so a
  high-frequency tiling texture stops aliasing frame-to-frame at distance. Default 0 keeps existing samplers
  byte-identical. **LOD bias is a D3D11 / Vulkan feature; Metal's sampler has none and Veldrid throws on a
  non-zero bias, so `CreateSampler` feature-guards it to 0 when unsupported** (mirrors the existing anisotropy
  fallback) - the sampler still builds on Metal, it just misses the extra distance blur there.
- **Terrain sampler** (`ModelRenderer`, the splat/terrain pipeline) now uses `maximumAnisotropy: 16` (was 8) and
  `mipLodBias: 1`. Anisotropy covers the grazing-angle case (a floor viewed near-parallel); the bias nudges
  distant ground to a blurrier mip so a noisy albedo stops sparkling. This is a rendering-quality change to
  terrain only - the model/prop pass and its goldens are untouched. Note the underlying texture's own
  high-frequency content is the root cause of the shimmer; the sampler levers reduce it, they do not remove a
  too-noisy source texture.

## 9.4.0

Per-cell world-state persistence: a `ShardHost` cell's authoritative non-player entities (mobs, resource nodes, dropped items) now survive a server restart, keyed per cell in an `IWorldStore`. Reuses the existing Replication snapshot codec, so any registered component persists. Additive minor, new public API.

- **`KhaozEngine.Sharding`** gains cell snapshot/restore primitives (no storage dependency): `CellSim.SnapshotOwned(IReadOnlySet<int> excludedNetIds)` snapshots a cell's owned (non-ghost, non-migrating) entities whose NetId is not excluded, `CellSim.RestoreOwned(byte[])` adopts a snapshot back as owned entities keeping their NetIds, and `CellSim.MaxOwnedNetId()` reports the highest owned id. `ShardHost.CellCreated` (an event raised once per cell on first instantiation, from any creation path) is the load hook, and `ShardHost.EnsureCell(CellCoord)` instantiates a cell by coordinate.
- **`KhaozEngine.NetWorld`** gains the persistence wiring: `CellPersistence` + `CellPersistenceConfig` drive an `IWorldStore` through the new `ICellPersistenceHost` seam, with lazy load-on-cell-create applied on the server thread, a periodic dirty save of changed cells, `PreloadAsync`/`LoadMetaAsync`/`FlushAsync`, and a `WorldMetaRecord` NetId high-water mark so a restored entity can never collide with a freshly spawned player. A versioned blob header (`CellPersistenceConfig.SchemaVersion`) skips a save it cannot safely decode rather than mis-reading it. `ShardedWorldServer` implements `ICellPersistenceHost`.
- Players stay out of scope (already persisted player-keyed by `WorldPersistence`); ghosts and migrating entities are excluded. Cell records are keyed `cell:{x}:{y}`, the NetId high-water under `world:meta`, both distinct from the existing `player:` keys.
- `MmoServerSample` gains a `ResourceNode` component and `CellPersistence` wiring, with a `--persistence-demo` run that spawns a node, restarts onto the same store, and restores it.

## 9.3.0
